lines.japanese: そう―――静かな朝である。
lines.english: Yes—a quiet morning.

lines.japanese: 「……今朝は、特に静かだね」
lines.english: “…It's especially quiet this morning.”

lines.japanese:
誰ともなく言った。
　葉子と斎が顔を合わせた。
lines.english: He said it to no one in particular. Youko and Itsuki exchanged a glance.

lines.japanese: 「……ご存じなさげ？」
lines.english: “…You don't seem to have heard?”

lines.japanese: 「って？」
lines.english: “Know what?”

lines.japanese: 「昨日の日曜は、大変だったのです」
lines.english: “Yesterday—Sunday—was quite an ordeal.”

lines.japanese: 斎がうんうんと頷く。
lines.english: Itsuki nodded emphatically.

lines.japanese: 「こっちも昨日は大変だったんだ」
lines.english: “We had quite a day yesterday too.”

lines.japanese:
「遊んでたら、あずさのお母さんにまとめて
　叱られた」
lines.english: “We were playing when Azusa's mom came over and scolded the whole lot of us.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、またドジったのか？」
lines.english: “You screw up again?”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、はははは……」
lines.english: “Ahaha, hahaha…”

lines.japanese: 肩を落とす。
lines.english: Her shoulders slumped.

lines.japanese:
「……だって、お母さん出てきたらしょうが
　ないジャン……最終兵器だよ……」
lines.english: “…Once Mom shows up, it's game over, y'know… She's the ultimate weapon…”

lines.japanese: 「難儀だな。あの女、美人なのに」
lines.english: “Tough break. That woman’s a beauty, though.”

lines.japanese: 「おーーーーーーいっ！！」
lines.english: “Heeeeeey!”

lines.japanese: 「なんだ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「人の母親をあの女呼ばわりすんなよ！」
lines.english: “Don't call someone else's mother ‘that woman’!”

lines.japanese: 「美人なのは事実だ」
lines.english: “She's beautiful. That's a fact.”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんか胸のあたりがもにょもにょするー！？」
lines.english: “S-something about that makes my chest feel all squirmy?!”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと棘がある印象だけど、美人だよね」
lines.english: “She's a little prickly, but she is beautiful.”

lines.japanese: 「いい女だ」
lines.english: “She's one fine woman.”

lines.japanese:
「だからそういう話されると娘としてもやもやする
　んですけど……」
lines.english: “I'm her daughter, and this whole conversation is making me seriously uncomfortable…”

lines.japanese:
「事によったら、おまえの父親になることだってあ
　り得る」
lines.english: “Depending on how this plays out, I might even wind up your father.”

lines.japanese:
「そそそそれだけは
　やめれッッッ！！」
lines.english: “J-just—whatever you do, don't do that!!”

lines.japanese:
臀部にがしがし蹴りが入るが、樋口章二、意に介
さず。
lines.english: She landed kick after kick on his backside, but Shouji Higuchi paid them no mind.

lines.japanese: 「何の話だったかな」
lines.english: “What were we talking about?”

lines.japanese: 「私が忍さんと楽しくお話を―――」
lines.english: “I was having a lovely conversation with Shinobu—”

lines.japanese:
「そういやな、オレのバイト先に来てたぞ、
　おまえの母親」
lines.english: “Speaking of which, your mother came by my part-time job.”

lines.japanese: 「うそ？」
lines.english: “You're kidding.”

lines.japanese: 「挨拶しておいた。サービスもしておいた」
lines.english: “I said hello. Gave her a little extra service, too.”

lines.japanese: 「あずさのお母さんの職場って」
lines.english: “Azusa, your mother's workplace is…”

lines.japanese: 「……駅の向こう……」
lines.english: “…On the other side of the station…”

lines.japanese: 「あり得るね」
lines.english: “Then it could've happened.”

lines.japanese: 「事実あった」
lines.english: “It did happen.”

lines.japanese: 「……まさか……く、口説いたり……した？」
lines.english: “…You didn't… h-hit on her… did you?”

lines.japanese: 「どうだろうな」
lines.english: “Who knows?”

lines.japanese: 章二は唇の端を吊り上げ、ニヤリと笑う。
lines.english: One corner of Shouji's mouth curled into a smirk.

lines.japanese: 「うわー、母親が寝取られるー！」
lines.english: “Oh no! He's stealing my mom!”

lines.japanese: 「焦るな、息子よ」
lines.english: “Don't panic, my son.”

lines.japanese: 「娘だろっ！！」
lines.english: “I'm your daughter!”

lines.japanese: 「父親として娘・あずさを飼育するうちに―――」
lines.english: “As your father, while I tend and feed my daughter Azusa—”

lines.japanese: 「養育だ！」
lines.english: “It's called raising a child!”

lines.japanese:
「―――ちゃんと女を証明するパーツが生えてくる
　のか？　胸とか尻とか」
lines.english: “—will she finally grow the parts that prove she's a woman? Boobs, a butt, that kind of thing?”

lines.japanese: 「植物かあたしは……」
lines.english: “What am I, a plant?”

lines.japanese: 「違ったものが生えてきたりしてな」
lines.english: “Maybe something else will sprout instead.”

lines.japanese: 笑われた意味をあずさは理解できない。
lines.english: Azusa did not understand the joke at her expense.

lines.japanese: 「な、なんだよう、違ったものって……？」
lines.english: “Wh-what do you mean, ‘something else’…?”

lines.japanese: 「……聞いてはならない」
lines.english: “…Do not ask.”

lines.japanese: 「ふえ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「沙也加にメッされるよ」
lines.english: “Sayaka will tell you that's naughty.”

lines.japanese: 「う、わかんないけどわかった……」
lines.english: “I don't get it, but I get it…”

lines.japanese: この世は、あずさの知らないことでいっぱいだった。
lines.english: The world was full of things Azusa did not know.

lines.japanese: 「で、なんだっけ？」
lines.english: “So, where were we?”

lines.japanese: 「昨日大事件が―――」
lines.english: “There was a major incident yesterday—”

lines.japanese: 「また兄妹喧嘩でもしたのか」
lines.english: “Did you two have another sibling squabble?”

lines.japanese:
「しました。しかしそれは大事件でもなんでもない
　日常と言えましょう」
lines.english: “We did. But that hardly qualifies as a major incident. You might call it an ordinary day.”

lines.japanese: 「あんま想像できないね」
lines.english: “I have trouble picturing it.”

lines.japanese: 「確かに」
lines.english: “True.”

lines.japanese: 「どんな喧嘩なんだ？　原因は？」
lines.english: “What does a fight between you two look like? What started it?”

lines.japanese:
「このムッツリが、人が乏しいお小遣いから買った
　ブルーマウンテンの粉を勝手に使ったばかりか」
lines.english: “This brooding lout not only helped himself to the Blue Mountain coffee I bought with my meager allowance…”

lines.japanese:
「開けっ放しにして香りを逃がしたのでぶったら、
　殴る蹴るなどの暴行を加えてきました」
lines.english: “He left the bag open and let the aroma escape, and when I smacked him for it, he retaliated with punches, kicks, and other violence.”

lines.japanese: 「小物かおまえら」
lines.english: “How petty can the two of you get?”

lines.japanese:
「この男を野放しにしておくと、セカイがアブナイ
　気が……」
lines.english: “I feel that allowing this man to roam free puts the entire WORLD in DANGER…”

lines.japanese: 「殴る蹴るって……」
lines.english: “Punches and kicks…?”

lines.japanese: 「がしがしと。割とその、性別とか忘れてる感じで」
lines.english: “Pretty hard. Like, uh, he’d forgotten I was a girl.”

lines.japanese: 「ひどいですよね？」
lines.english: “Isn't that awful?”

lines.japanese: 「ええーと」
lines.english: “Um…”

lines.japanese: 「斎くん、なんか目の回りにアザがあるね」
lines.english: “Itsuki, you've got a bruise around your eye.”

lines.japanese: 「葉子ちゃん勝ったんだ？」
lines.english: “So you won, Youko?”

lines.japanese: 「仲良くケンカしなね」
lines.english: “Fight nice, you two.”
“…Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「で、なんだっけ？」
lines.english: “So, where were we?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでしたっけ？」
lines.english: “Where were we?”

lines.japanese: 「大変だった昨日の話じゃないのか」
lines.english: “Weren't you telling us about yesterday's major incident?”

lines.japanese:
「ああ、実は昨日、女３人で紅茶のお店に行った時
　に―――」
lines.english: “Oh, yes. Yesterday, three of us girls went out for tea, and—”

lines.japanese:
と、斎の目がもの言いたげに向けられていること
に、忍は気付いた。
lines.english: That was when Shinobu noticed Itsuki looking at him as if he had something to say.

lines.japanese: 「え？　斎も主張したいことがあるって？」
lines.english: “What? You have a case you'd like to make too, Itsuki?”

lines.japanese: 頷く。
lines.english: He nodded.

lines.japanese: 「で、なに？」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　やっぱりいい？」
lines.english: “Huh? Changed your mind?”

lines.japanese: 「またの機会にする？　でも微妙に気になるよ」
lines.english: “We can save it for next time, but now I'm kind of curious.”

lines.japanese:
「僕の気持ちだけでもう充分だって？
　水くさいこと言うじゃないか」
lines.english: “My feelings alone are enough for you? Don't be such a stranger.”

lines.japanese:
男同士の友情臭さを存分にまとわりつかせ、忍と
斎は見つめ合った。
lines.english: The reek of male friendship hanging thick around them, Shinobu and Itsuki gazed into each other's eyes.

lines.japanese: 「長時間に渡ってスルーされている最中なわけです」
lines.english: “Meanwhile, I’ve been ignored for quite some time now.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめん……」
lines.english: “Sorry…”

lines.japanese: 「昨日の事件って言うと、アレか。猟奇殺人事件」
lines.english: “Yesterday's incident? You mean the bizarre murder case.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことがあったの？　てゅか、何それ？」
lines.english: “Wait, that happened? I mean, what even is that?”

lines.japanese:
「オレ様も詳しくは知らんがな。なんでもこの街で
　凶器を用いた殺人事件が起こったらしい」
lines.english: “I don't know the details myself. Apparently there was a murder in town involving some kind of weapon.”

lines.japanese:
「犯人はまだ捕まっていないってことだが……
　なんだ葉子、その目は」
lines.english: “They say the culprit hasn't been caught yet… What's with that look, Youko?”

lines.japanese: 「……おのれ」
lines.english: “…Damn you.”

lines.japanese: 「なんなんだおまえは」
lines.english: “What is your problem?”

lines.japanese: 「物騒だな。凶器って何さ？」
lines.english: “That's disturbing. What was the weapon?”

lines.japanese: 「そこまでは知らん」
lines.english: “I don't know that much.”

lines.japanese:
「ねえねえ、今朝、人が少ないのって
　もしかして……」
lines.english: “Hey, hey. Could there be so few people around this morning because of that…?”

lines.japanese:
「だな。自主休校なり休暇なり取ってるヤツが多い
　んだろう。こういうのも、日常化しちまったよう
　だな」
lines.english: “Probably. A lot of people must be staying home from school or taking time off. Looks like this sort of thing has become routine.”

lines.japanese:
「といっても、そんな連中が日中街で遊びほうけて
　いる場面を、オレはよく見るがな」
lines.english: “Though I often see those same people goofing around town in broad daylight anyway.”

lines.japanese: 「ぜんぶ話された……」
lines.english: “He told them everything…”

lines.japanese: 「さっきからなんだ葉子」
lines.english: “What have you been muttering about this whole time, Youko?”

lines.japanese: 「好感度が、稼げない」
lines.english: “I'm not gaining any affection points.”

lines.japanese: 「わけがわからん」
lines.english: “I have no idea what you're talking about.”

lines.japanese:
「あたし、なんとなくわかる……
　章二は天然でいじわるだ」
lines.english: “I think I kind of get it… Shouji's mean without even realizing it.”

lines.japanese: 「普通に話しただけだ」
lines.english: “All I did was talk normally.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　だから葉子はバカなんだって？」
lines.english: “Huh? You're saying that's why Youko is so dumb?”
“Hmph.”

lines.japanese: ぼかぼかぼか（葉子→斎）。
lines.english: Whap whap whap (Youko → Itsuki).

lines.japanese: ぽかぽかぽか（斎→葉子）。
lines.english: Bap bap bap (Itsuki → Youko).

lines.japanese: 兄妹喧嘩がはじまった。
lines.english: The sibling squabble began.

lines.japanese: 「けんか雲出てる」
lines.english: “They've got a fight cloud.”

lines.japanese: 「子供のケンカだ」
lines.english: “They're fighting like little kids.”

lines.japanese: 「仲悪いんだか良いんだか……」
lines.english: “I can't tell whether they get along or hate each other…”

lines.japanese: しかし二人とも、忍の大切な仲間である。
lines.english: Yet both were companions he held dear.

lines.japanese: 「うっ、んっ」
lines.english: “Ungh… nn!”

lines.japanese:
結構容赦なくばちばち叩いている。
　怪我しない程度、でも限度いっぱいに苦痛がある
ように。
lines.english: They slapped at each other with very little restraint. Not hard enough to injure, but inflicting as much pain as they could without crossing that line.

lines.japanese: 放っておいても良さそうだと忍は判断した。
lines.english: Shinobu decided it seemed all right to leave them to it.

lines.japanese: 「……やれやれ」
lines.english: “…Good grief.”

lines.japanese:
自然、口元が微笑を宿す。
　そういえば二人と出会ったのはいつだったろう？
　ふと記憶を手繰ってみる。
lines.english: He found himself smiling. Come to think of it, when had he first met the two of them? He reached back through his memory.

lines.japanese:
まだ若輩としか言えないその人生を半分に割ると
……ちょうど彼女と出会った頃になるだろう。
lines.english: If he divided his short life in half… the midpoint would fall almost exactly when he met her.

lines.japanese: 塚本葉子と出会い、はじめて言葉を交わした瞬間。
lines.english: The moment he met Youko Tsukamoto and spoke to her for the first time.

lines.japanese:
忍が未成熟だった日。
　当時はまだ、どんな不安もなかった。
　予兆も見えていなかった。
lines.english: Back when Shinobu was still immature. He had known no anxiety then. He had yet to glimpse the portents.

lines.japanese: 忍は葉子を、口説きに行った―――
lines.english: Shinobu went to win Youko over—

lines.japanese: 校庭の一角には、兎小屋があった。
lines.english: In one corner of the schoolyard stood a rabbit hutch.

lines.japanese:
安普請もいいところで、お世辞にも住み心地が良
いとは思えなかったが、否応もなく兎たちはそこに
生きていく。
lines.english: It was the shoddiest sort of construction, scarcely what anyone could call comfortable. Even so, the rabbits had no choice but to live there.

lines.japanese:
彼らに選択肢はない。
　それは人間も何ら変わりなく、選べるように見え
て人生の結果は一つしかない。
lines.english: They had no choice. Human beings were no different. Choice might appear to exist, but every life arrived at only one outcome.

lines.japanese:
確定の問題を置けば、人生は一本道であり、決ま
っているとも言えた。
lines.english: Leaving aside the question of predetermination, life was a single road; one could call its course fixed.

lines.japanese:
貴宮忍は自由意志に価値を見いださない。
　馬鹿にしてもいなかったが、とりたてて実りある
要素だとも思わなかった。
lines.english: Shinobu Atemiya found no value in free will. He did not scorn it; he simply did not think it particularly fruitful.

lines.japanese:
左右の道は等しかった。
　自由も束縛も等価値だった。
　孤も群も差はなかった。
lines.english: The roads to left and right were equal. Freedom and confinement had equal value. The solitary and the collective were no different.

lines.japanese:
個人の主観を入れなければ、苦しみはない。
　運命に限らず、何かに支配されることは自然なこ
とだ。
lines.english: Without individual subjectivity, there could be no suffering. Being ruled by something—fate or anything else—was perfectly natural.

lines.japanese: どの個体も全宇宙に等しくはないのだから―――
lines.english: For no single being equaled the universe as a whole—

lines.japanese:
含有される存在は全て、何かの下位に位置する。
　外圧や倫理や規則や運命や使命に、操られている。
lines.english: Every being contained within it stood beneath something else. All were controlled by external pressure, ethics, rules, fate, or duty.

lines.japanese:
操るもの。それは往々にして敵だ。
　人は自由でなければならないという言説は高らかだ。
lines.english: That which controlled them was often their enemy. The doctrine that human beings must be free rang out loud and clear.

lines.japanese:
だがある種の民が安全に支配されることを望み、
自由を放棄する自由を行使するに至っては、なにや
ら笑い話のオチのようにも思えてしまう。
lines.english: Yet some people wanted the safety of being ruled and exercised their freedom to surrender their freedom. By then, it had begun to sound like the punch line to a joke.

lines.japanese:
確かにそれも自由には違いない。
　近代化は個人意識の拡大だ。
　そして分割できる倫理は一定である。
lines.english: That, too, was certainly freedom. Modernization meant the expansion of individual consciousness. And the amount of ethics available to divide remained constant.

lines.japanese:
世界というラウンド・ケーキは一見均等に切り分
けられ、分配される。
lines.english: The round cake called the world appeared to be cut into equal slices and handed out.

lines.japanese:
人の望む権利という名の自由はしかし、無限の欲
求を秘める。
lines.english: But the freedom people desired—the thing called rights—contained a bottomless appetite.

lines.japanese:
ケーキ一切れでは足りない。
　故にそれは、内的に深く深く浸透していくしかな
いものである。
lines.english: One slice of cake was not enough. And so that hunger could only burrow deeper and deeper within.

lines.japanese:
人には権利がある。
　責任という御旗。
lines.english: People had rights. Responsibility was their banner.

lines.japanese:
無謀な行動をとっても良い。
　外国に行って傭兵となっても良い。
lines.english: People were free to act recklessly. Free to go abroad and become mercenaries.

lines.japanese:
近代は安楽死の自由を認めるかも知れない。
　近代は自殺を自由に含めるかも知れない。
lines.english: Modernity might recognize a freedom to choose euthanasia. Modernity might count suicide among its freedoms.

lines.japanese:
内的沈潜は個室化を生むことがある。
　人の心に踏み込む行為は悪だ、と入相の鐘をかき
鳴らす。
lines.english: Inward retreat could produce a world of private rooms. The evening bell rang out its warning: to trespass into another person's heart was evil.

lines.japanese:
そう、高度成長の輝きを喪失した近代とは、黄昏
と同義である。
lines.english: Modernity, then, stripped of the brilliance of rapid growth, was another name for twilight.

lines.japanese:
各人の心が聖域化していく。
　だが一人は寂しい。
　メッセージを投げかけねばならない。
lines.english: Each person's heart was becoming a sanctuary. But being alone was lonely. A message had to be sent.

lines.japanese:
出来うるならば高密度に凝縮された自意識を持っ
て、他者に衝撃・影響を与えたい。
lines.english: If possible, one wanted that sense of self compressed to its highest density— something powerful enough to strike another person and leave a mark.

lines.japanese:
発信型メディア―――ネットワークが十全な環境
を与えた。
lines.english: The network, a medium built for transmission, provided the ideal environment.

lines.japanese:
ではネットワークによる人類の結合という幻想は、
そもそも―――
lines.english: Then, from the very beginning, the fantasy of humanity united by the network was—

lines.japanese:
などと、大人たちが会話をしていたことがあって、
忍はそこに言葉遊びを感じた。
lines.english: Adults had once talked that way, and Shinobu had sensed a play on words in it.

lines.japanese:
職員室だったかと思う。
　それは教師たちの会話内容だ。
lines.english: He thought it had been in the faculty room. A conversation among teachers.

lines.japanese:
人の権利と侵害について、忍は思う。
　正解と禁止事項がわかれば良い。
lines.english: Shinobu considered human rights and their violation. All he needed was the right answer and a list of prohibitions.

lines.japanese:
個人の権利によって守られるものなど、忍にはど
うでも良いのだった。
lines.english: Whatever those individual rights were meant to protect, Shinobu did not care.

lines.japanese: 貴宮忍の血は冷たい。
lines.english: The blood in Shinobu Atemiya's veins was cold.

lines.japanese:
兎小屋には一耳の兎。
　名前は知らない。
lines.english: There were rabbits in the hutch. He did not know their names.

lines.japanese:
それぞれ別個の場所で、冷たい床にうずくまって、
もこもことした球体に変形している。
lines.english: Each huddled in its own place on the cold floor, curled into a fluffy ball.

lines.japanese: 寝ているのだ。
lines.english: They were asleep.

lines.japanese:
どことなく、自分と似たものを感じた。
　親しみは感じない。
lines.english: He saw something of himself in them. He felt no affection for them.

lines.japanese:
ウサギは小屋にいるが、忍は今世界にいる。
　個室ではない場所に放り出されて、日は浅い。
lines.english: The rabbits had their hutch; Shinobu now stood out in the world. He had only recently been cast into a place that was not a private room.

lines.japanese:
周囲に人間はいくらでもいるが、友達はいなかった。
　有り体に言えば、編入されたばかりだったのだ。
lines.english: There were people everywhere, but he had no friends. Put simply, he had only just transferred here.

lines.japanese:
だから外界に立っていてもなお、周囲の風景はソ
フトフォーカスでもかけたかのように遠い。
lines.english: Even standing here in the world outside, everything around him seemed remote, as if shot in soft focus.

lines.japanese:
昼休み。
　給食後のもっとも長い空き時間を、忍は持てあま
している。
lines.english: Lunch recess. Shinobu has no idea how to fill the longest free stretch of the school day, after lunch.

lines.japanese:
校庭には子供たちが大勢いる。遊んでいる。
　思い思いに集団を作り、ボールを追ったり闇雲に
走り回ったりしており、興奮による奇声も絶えない。
lines.english: The schoolyard is full of children at play. They have gathered into groups, chasing balls or racing blindly around, and their excited shrieks never stop.

lines.japanese:
その中で、風変わりなひと組を、先ほどからずっ
と視野におさめている。
lines.english: For some time now, one peculiar pair among them has held his attention.

lines.japanese:
兄妹だ。
　名を、塚本斎と塚本葉子。
lines.english: They are brother and sister. Itsuki Tsukamoto and Youko Tsukamoto.

lines.japanese:
斎の方は同級生。葉子は一つ下の学年だ。
　彼らのことは、知っている。
lines.english: Itsuki is in Shinobu's grade. Youko is one grade below him. He knows of them.

lines.japanese: たまにしか姿を見せない兄妹。
lines.english: The siblings who rarely appear.

lines.japanese:
校内でも知らない者はほとんどいないだろう。
　兄の斎はそうでもないが、妹の方はたまにしか来
ない。
lines.english: Almost everyone at school must know of them. Itsuki, the older brother, attends somewhat more regularly, but his sister appears only once in a while.

lines.japanese: 病弱、という理由。
lines.english: They say it is because she is frail.

lines.japanese:
忍は見る。葉子を。
　病弱、と言われればそう見えないこともない。
　どちらかというと、薄いのである。
lines.english: Shinobu studies Youko. Told that she is frail, he can believe it. More than frail, though, she seems faint.

lines.japanese:
存在が薄い。
　個性に欠けているのではない。
　定義が難しい。
lines.english: Her very existence seems faint. Not that she lacks personality. It is difficult to define.

lines.japanese:
中性的な少女である。
　顔立ちが整っているせいで、そう見える。
　兄は精悍な印象。
lines.english: She is an androgynous girl. Her fine, symmetrical features create that impression. Her brother looks lean and rugged.

lines.japanese:
どちらも無駄がない。
　二人に通底するのは、無機質の何か。
　忍同様、登校頻度の低い二人だ。友人はいない。
lines.english: There is nothing superfluous about either of them. Something inorganic underlies them both. Like Shinobu, neither attends often. Neither has friends.

lines.japanese:
兄妹でキャッチボールをしている。
　グローブも使わない、ゴムボールでのキャッチだ。
lines.english: The siblings are playing catch. No gloves; only a rubber ball.

lines.japanese:
兄はそれなりに様になっているが、葉子の方は
稚拙である。
lines.english: The brother looks practiced enough, but Youko is clumsy.

lines.japanese: 取り逃がしも多い。
lines.english: She misses often.

lines.japanese:
後方に飛んでいったボールを追い、拾い、兄に投
げる。
lines.english: She chases a ball that flies behind her, retrieves it, and throws it back to her brother.

lines.japanese:
兄は兄で淡々と受け、妹に投げ返す。こちらに
ミスはない。
lines.english: Her brother catches it with the same impassive calm and throws it back. He never misses.

lines.japanese:
妹がなんとか取って、表情も変えずにまた兄
に―――
lines.english: Somehow, his sister catches it and, expressionless, sends it back to him—

lines.japanese: （なんか……事務作業みたいだ……）
lines.english: (It's like… paperwork…)

lines.japanese:
楽しんでいる雰囲気はない。
　ボール投げという行為だけを、心を込めずになぞっ
ているように思えた。
lines.english: There is no sense that either is enjoying it. They seem to be tracing the bare motions of throwing a ball, putting no feeling into them.

lines.japanese: （あの二人……なんだろう……）
lines.english: (What is it… with those two…?)

lines.japanese: （見てると……泣きそうになってくる）
lines.english: (Watching them… makes me feel like crying.)

lines.japanese:
それでも忍は、感慨を表情に出すこともなく、見
守っている。
lines.english: Even so, Shinobu watches without allowing the feeling to show on his face.

lines.japanese:
彼のいる場所は小屋のそばで、死角であった。
　てんてんと、ゴムボールが転がってきた。
　忍のつま先に当たって止まる。
lines.english: He stands in a blind spot beside the hutch. The rubber ball comes bouncing toward him. It taps his toe and stops.

lines.japanese:
視線を上げると、葉子が兎小屋の向こう側にまわ
ろうとしていた。
lines.english: When he looks up, Youko is starting around the far side of the rabbit hutch.

lines.japanese: （そっちじゃないよ。ここだよ）
lines.english: (Not that way. It's here.)

lines.japanese: 何か思ったにせよ、言葉もない忍だ。
lines.english: He thinks it, but says nothing.

lines.japanese: 逡巡。
lines.english: He hesitates.

lines.japanese: 結局、ボールを拾い上げた。
lines.english: In the end, he picks up the ball.

lines.japanese:
途端、どっと心臓が跳ねた。
　緊張のためである。
lines.english: His heart immediately gives a violent leap. Nerves.

lines.japanese:
（うわ……うまく話せそうにない……
　どうしよう……）
lines.english: (Oh no… I don't think I can speak properly… What do I do…?)

lines.japanese:
しかし拾ってしまった。
　接触しなければならない。
lines.english: But he has picked it up now. Now he has to make contact.

lines.japanese: 接触！
lines.english: Contact!

lines.japanese:
それは貴宮忍にとって、なんとベールに包まれた
行動であったろう。
lines.english: To Shinobu Atemiya, making contact is an act veiled in mystery.

lines.japanese:
薄く見える稜線以上の遠きに、触れあいという行
為がさも聖なるものであるかのように掲げられている。
太陽か月のようにだ。
lines.english: Beyond even the faint ridge on the horizon, the act of human contact stands enshrined as something sacred— like the sun or moon.

lines.japanese:
そんなものを、手に取らねばならない。
　気が遠くなる。
　幸い、斎はじっと元の場所で待機している。
lines.english: Now he must reach out and grasp it. The prospect makes his head swim. Fortunately, Itsuki remains where he is, waiting.

lines.japanese: （……よし。今なら一人を相手にすればすむや）
lines.english: (…Good. This way I only have to deal with one of them.)

lines.japanese:
兎小屋に向かう。
　金網ごしに、ボールを探している葉子が見えた。
lines.english: He approaches the rabbit hutch. Through the wire, he sees Youko searching for the ball.

lines.japanese:
前方に躍り出た忍の姿に、葉子が小首をかしげた。
　近くで見ると、思ったよりあどけない。
lines.english: When Shinobu suddenly steps into view, Youko tips her head to one side. Up close, she looks more childlike than he expected.

lines.japanese:
何も言えない。
　忍の頭は真っ白になっている。
lines.english: He cannot say a word. Shinobu's mind is blank.

lines.japanese: （この子の目……すごく深い―――）
lines.english: (Her eyes… they're so deep—)

lines.japanese: 何秒もの間、厳めしい顔つきで、忍は静止していた。
lines.english: For several seconds, Shinobu stands rigid, a stern look on his face.

lines.japanese: （……いけない、おかしい人だって思われる）
lines.english: (…This is bad. She'll think I'm strange.)

lines.japanese: 心中せき立てられて、ボールを差し出す。
lines.english: Urged on by his thoughts, he holds out the ball.

lines.japanese:
葉子は両手でボールを受け取る。
　忍を見る。
lines.english: Youko accepts the ball in both hands. She looks at Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
目を見ている感じではない。
　忍全体を、ぼんやりと眺めていた。
lines.english: She does not seem to be looking him in the eyes. Her unfocused gaze takes in all of him at once.

lines.japanese:
そして不意に、兄のもとに走り去る。
　突発的な行動だが、忍は安堵した。
　ストレスが遠ざかっていく。
lines.english: Then, without warning, she runs back to her brother. Her sudden departure leaves Shinobu relieved. The tension drains out of him as she goes.

lines.japanese: （……結局、何も言えなかった……）
lines.english: (…In the end, I couldn't say anything…)

lines.japanese:
じっと見送る向こう、少女の肩越しに兄の視線が、
忍を射抜く。
lines.english: As Shinobu watches her go, her brother's gaze lances over the girl's shoulder and straight through him.
(…That was…)

lines.japanese:
敵意も感じないが、好意も見えない。
　機械的であった。
lines.english: There is no hostility in it, but no goodwill either. The gaze is mechanical.

lines.japanese: （変な兄妹―――）
lines.english: (What a strange pair of siblings—)

lines.japanese: 忍もまた、人のことは言えない。
lines.english: Shinobu is hardly one to talk.

lines.japanese: 帰宅も兄妹一緒だった。忍は彼らのあとを追った。
lines.english: The siblings went home together, too. Shinobu followed them.

lines.japanese: 二十メートルも背後を歩く。
lines.english: He walked some twenty meters behind them.

lines.japanese: （なぜ追いかけてるんだ……？）
lines.english: (Why am I following them…?)

lines.japanese: 惑いが忍をさいなんでいる。
lines.english: Confusion gnawed at him.

lines.japanese:
その思考が、距離となってあらわれている。
　縮む様子はない。つもりも。
　相手に合わせた足取りは緻密で、自動的だった。
lines.english: His uncertainty took physical form in the distance between them. It showed no sign of shrinking. He had no intention of shrinking it. He matched their pace with precise, automatic steps.

lines.japanese: （どうして、あの二人が気になる……？）
lines.english: (Why do I care about those two…?)

lines.japanese:
考えるまでもなかった。
　忍には友人が必要だ。
　友人にならなければならない。
lines.english: He did not need to think about it. Shinobu needed friends. He had to make friends with them.

lines.japanese:
大きな目的意識だ。
　強迫観念にも近い。
　なぜならば、彼らも忍と同類だからだ。
lines.english: It was a powerful sense of purpose. Close to an obsession. Because they were the same kind as Shinobu.

lines.japanese: 忍自身が誰よりもよく知っていた。
lines.english: Shinobu knew it better than anyone.

lines.japanese:
やがて二人はより高級な住宅街に入っていく。
　何名かの要人が住んでいる区画だ。
lines.english: Eventually, the pair entered a more exclusive residential district. Several prominent figures lived there.

lines.japanese:
建て売りの住宅は消え、背の高い壁で広い敷地を
囲んだ家が増える。
lines.english: The tract houses gave way to large properties enclosed by high walls.

lines.japanese: 兄妹はその一つに近づく。
lines.english: The siblings approached one of them.

lines.japanese: （金持ち？）
lines.english: (Rich people?)

lines.japanese:
巨大な門……の横手にもうけられた通用門から、
敷地内に入った。
lines.english: They entered through the enormous gate… or rather, through the side entrance built beside it.

lines.japanese:
ドアフォンを押していた。
　許可がなければ庭にも入れないということだろう。
lines.english: They rang the intercom. Apparently, even the garden was off-limits without permission.

lines.japanese: （うーん）
lines.english: (Hmm.)

lines.japanese:
周辺をぐるっと見回ってみる。
　……驚くほど広い土地だった。
lines.english: He walked the entire perimeter. …The grounds were astonishingly vast.

lines.japanese:
屋敷を覆う壁は切れ目もなく、高すぎて内側をう
かがうこともできない。
lines.english: The wall around the estate ran unbroken and stood too high for him to see inside.

lines.japanese:
途中、壁際に和風建築を模して瓦をあしらった掲
示板があり、そこには屋敷が由緒ある建物であるこ
とが古い書体で説明されていた。
lines.english: Partway around, beside the wall, stood a tiled noticeboard designed to resemble traditional Japanese architecture. In old-fashioned script, it recounted the mansion's distinguished history.

lines.japanese: （明治時代から要人御用達……か）
lines.english: (Favored by dignitaries since the Meiji era…)

lines.japanese: ついつい、ため息が出た。
lines.english: A sigh slipped out.

lines.japanese:
（大御所だ。お坊ちゃんだ。お嬢様だ。
　浮世離れだ。金持ちだ）
lines.english: (Big shots. A young master. A young lady. A world apart. Rich people.)

lines.japanese: そんなのと友達にならねばならない。
lines.english: Those were the people he had to befriend.

lines.japanese:
忍は立ち尽くした。
　そんなのと友達にならねばならない。
lines.english: Shinobu stood rooted to the spot. Those were the people he had to befriend.

lines.japanese: 「どうやって―――？」
lines.english: “How am I supposed to—?”

lines.japanese:
塚本兄妹は一週間、学校を休んだ。
　貴宮忍は、お屋敷への侵入を決意した。
lines.english: The Tsukamoto siblings were absent from school for a week. Shinobu Atemiya decided to infiltrate the estate.

lines.japanese: （……なんで……こんなことしてるんだろう……）
lines.english: (…Why am I… doing this…?)

lines.japanese:
見つかったら洒落では済まない。本来は。
　子供であるなら、言い訳もつくだろう。
lines.english: If caught, he would normally be in serious trouble. As a child, though, he could probably make an excuse.

lines.japanese:
リスクとしてはさほどでもない。
　やらない手はなかった。
lines.english: The risk was not especially great. There was no reason not to try.

lines.japanese: 第一関門である壁は乗り越えた。
lines.english: He scaled the wall, his first obstacle.

lines.japanese:
レーザーやカメラが仕掛けられているということ
もなく、敷地内にドーベルマンが放し飼いにされて
もいなかった。
lines.english: No lasers or cameras had been installed, nor were Dobermans roaming loose around the grounds.

lines.japanese: （問題は……）
lines.english: (The problem is…)

lines.japanese:
潜入してどうするか。
　兄妹が目的なのだが、会いに行って会話をしよう
とは思っていない。
lines.english: What would he do now that he was inside? The siblings were his objective, but he had no intention of simply walking up and talking to them.

lines.japanese:
さすがの忍も、それで友人関係が築けるとは考え
てはいなかった。
lines.english: Even Shinobu did not think that would be enough to make friends.

lines.japanese: （……情報集め）
lines.english: (…Gather intelligence.)

lines.japanese:
接触の機会があまりにも少ない。
　兄妹の好みや、習い事も知らない。
　話しかけるのは学校を置いて他にない。
lines.english: Opportunities for contact were far too scarce. He knew neither their interests nor what lessons they took. School was the only place he could approach them.

lines.japanese:
だがきっかけとなる会話の組み立てをするために
は、必要な個人情報が欠けていた。
lines.english: But to plan the conversation that might give him an opening, he lacked the personal information he needed.

lines.japanese:
そう、個人情報が大切なのである。
　防御壁を乗り越えて潜入した忍の目的は、諜報活動
にあった。
lines.english: Yes. Personal information was essential. Shinobu had breached the defenses and entered the grounds to conduct espionage.

lines.japanese: （いくでござる）
lines.english: (I sally forth.)

lines.japanese:
敷地内を歩く。
　壁際はちょっとした林になっている。
lines.english: He moved through the grounds. A thin belt of woodland ran along the wall.

lines.japanese:
茂みをかき分けて進むと、視界が開けた。
　玉砂利が敷かれ、池があり、建物があった。
lines.english: He pushed through the undergrowth, and the view opened up. Pebbles covered the ground; there was a pond and a building.

lines.japanese: （まるで武家屋敷だ）
lines.english: (It looks like a samurai mansion.)

lines.japanese:
そこには現代が欠けていた。
　時間の流れが粘性を帯びて沈殿し、動きを止めて
いるようでもある。
lines.english: The modern age was missing from this place. Time itself seemed to have grown viscous, settled to the bottom, and ceased to move.

lines.japanese:
琥珀に閉じこめられた過去を思わせた。
　忍は任務を忘れ、しばしいにしえの空気に圧倒さ
れた。
lines.english: It made him think of a past sealed in amber. Shinobu forgot his mission, overwhelmed for a moment by the air of antiquity.

lines.japanese: （いけない……こんなところにいたら見つかる）
lines.english: (No… If I stay out here, someone will see me.)

lines.japanese: すぐに茂みに上体を潜めた。
lines.english: He quickly hid his upper body in the bushes.

lines.japanese: （誰もいないな……人の気配もないし）
lines.english: (No one's here… I don't sense anyone, either.)

lines.japanese:
大勢の人間が住んでいるとは限らない。
　むしろこんな静閑には、大家族の騒々しさは似合
わない。
lines.english: Perhaps not many people lived here. In fact, the noise of a large family would have seemed out of place in such stillness.

lines.japanese: 声を発することが罪にも思える。
lines.english: Speaking aloud felt almost like a sin.

lines.japanese: （どっちにしても、出せないけど）
lines.english: (Not that I could anyway.)

lines.japanese: スパイ活動中だ。
lines.english: He was on a spy mission.

lines.japanese:
（そうだ……二人を捜そう。
　きっと自宅では遊んでいるはずだ）
lines.english: (Right… I'll find them. They must play when they're at home.)

lines.japanese:
幸い、茂みと林は壁に添ってぐるりと敷地を縁取
っている。
lines.english: Fortunately, brush and trees ringed the entire estate along the wall.

lines.japanese: （よし）
lines.english: (Good.)

lines.japanese: 忍は位置を変えた。
lines.english: Shinobu moved on.

lines.japanese:
ほとんど一周しても、建物の内側を見通せる箇所
は見つからなかった。
lines.english: He had almost circled the estate and still found nowhere from which he could see inside the house.

lines.japanese:
（縁側の下に隠れて、会話を拾うって手もある
　けど……）
lines.english: (I could hide under the veranda and listen in on their conversations…)

lines.japanese:
中庭に敷かれた玉砂利が気になる。
　忍の知識にはなかったが、踏めば音が出ることは
容易に想像できた。
lines.english: The gravel covering the courtyard worried him. He did not know what it was for, but could easily imagine the noise it would make underfoot.

lines.japanese: 音の伝達を緩和する方法を……少し考えて破棄した。
lines.english: He considered ways of muffling the sound for a moment… then discarded the idea.

lines.japanese:
（どこぞのスーパーくのいちじゃあるまいし、
　そんなことできるわけない……）
lines.english: (I'm not some superpowered lady ninja. There's no way I could pull that off…)

lines.japanese: （しかし、困ったな）
lines.english: (Still, this is a problem.)

lines.japanese: 動きが止まる。
lines.english: He came to a halt.

lines.japanese:
これでは内情がわからない。
　ずっと待機して、動きがあるのを待つべきだろうか。
lines.english: He would learn nothing this way. Should he stay here until something happened?

lines.japanese:
そんなことを考えていると、目の前にボールが転
がってきた。
lines.english: As he pondered the question, a ball came rolling to a stop before him.

lines.japanese:
一抱えもある大きなゴムボールだ。
　全身の筋肉が緊張に強ばる。
lines.english: It was a huge rubber ball, big enough to fill his arms. Every muscle in his body went rigid.

lines.japanese:
誰かがやってきて、ボールを拾った。
　細い足首が見えた。
lines.english: Someone came over and picked it up. He saw a pair of slender ankles.

lines.japanese: （このパターン―――）
lines.english: (This again—)

lines.japanese:
茂みの中だ。
　見つかるはずはない。
lines.english: He was inside the bushes. There was no way she could find him.

lines.japanese:
物音を立てなければ、向こうからこちらが見える
ことはない。
lines.english: So long as he made no sound, she could not possibly see him from where she stood.

lines.japanese: はずだった。
lines.english: That was how it should have been.

lines.japanese: しかし―――
lines.english: But—

lines.japanese:
ボールを拾った葉子は、最初から存在を知ってい
たかのように、茂みの中の忍を見た。
lines.english: Youko, ball in hand, looked straight at Shinobu in the bushes as though she had known he was there all along.

lines.japanese:
目が合った。
　少女の藍色をした瞳が、深みをもって忍を呑み込
もうとする。
lines.english: Their eyes met. The deep indigo of the girl's eyes seemed about to swallow Shinobu whole.

lines.japanese:
ただ、見返すことしかできなかった。
　葉子のそれが茫漠たる海だとすれば、忍の視線は
射られた矢だ。
lines.english: All he could do was stare back. If Youko's gaze was a boundless sea, Shinobu's was an arrow loosed into it.

lines.japanese:

lines.english: “Are you some kind of eccentric?”

lines.japanese: 「わからない」

lines.japanese: 「手際良かったな、潜入」

lines.japanese:

lines.english: “There is a dog.”

lines.english: “No. It's doing its job admirably.”

lines.english: Reserved though she was, Sayaka enjoyed flustering people. He had managed not to give himself away, yet he still felt as though she might be watching him from somewhere.

lines.japanese:
まだ三時前。
　思ったより早かったので、忍は安堵する。
lines.english: It was not even three yet. It was earlier than he had expected, which came as a relief.

lines.japanese:
今日は診察機材の関係で、街にある遠い方の病院
に行かねばならない。
lines.english: Because of the equipment needed for today’s examination, he had to go to the more distant hospital in town.

lines.japanese:
つま先を切り返す。
　沙也加とのんびり歩いてきた道を、急ぎ足で街に
戻った。
lines.english: He wheeled around. Then he hurried back toward town along the road he and Sayaka had just strolled down.

lines.japanese: 「ふう」
lines.english: “Whew.”

lines.japanese:
長い検査が終わり、ようやく解放された。
　異常なし、とのことで追検査もなく、少しだけ気
分が軽い。
lines.english: The long examination was over; at last he was free. Nothing abnormal had turned up, so there would be no follow-up tests. He felt a little lighter.

lines.japanese: 「夕方か……」
lines.english: “Evening already…”

lines.japanese:
微妙な時間だった。
　工場に行けば、誰かいるかも知れないが。
　すぐに解散することになるだろう。
lines.english: It was an awkward hour. There might still be someone at the factory, though. They would probably be leaving soon anyway.

lines.japanese:
空腹でもあるし、帰宅してもいいだろう。
　どこからか、焼き鳥の香りが漂ってきた。商店街
だろう。
lines.english: He was hungry; he might as well go home. The smell of grilled chicken skewers drifted from somewhere—probably the shopping district.

lines.japanese:
買い食いという選択肢が追加された。
　間で狂おしく取捨選択に懊悩していると、
lines.english: Buying a snack on the way home became another option. As he agonized absurdly over his choices—

lines.japanese:
シン、と空気が濁った。
　鈍感な忍ではあるが、関知せずにはいられないほ
どの……敵意。
lines.english: The air fell silent and murky. Even Shinobu, insensitive as he was, could not fail to sense it— hostility.

lines.japanese:
銃口を向けられた気分と似ていた。
　忍はじっと相手の出方を待った。
　自分に用事があるに、違いないからだ。
lines.english: It felt like having a gun pointed at him. Shinobu stood still and waited for the other person to make a move. They had business with him. Of that there was no doubt.

lines.japanese: 「よう、優等生」
lines.english: “Yo, honor student.”

lines.japanese:
親しげな挨拶。
　そんな体裁でありながら、唾棄するような言葉だ
った。
lines.english: A seemingly friendly greeting. Friendly in form alone—the words themselves were spat with contempt.

lines.japanese: 「……おまえのことは、よく覚えてるよ」
lines.english: “…I remember you well.”

lines.japanese: 「へぇ、マジかよ。そりゃありがてぇや」
lines.english: “Yeah? For real? I'm touched.”

lines.japanese:
背後。
　おそらくずっと以前から忍を発見していたのだ。
lines.english: Behind him. Whoever it was had probably spotted Shinobu long before.

lines.japanese:
そして意図的に、背後から接近した。
　本当に銃を持っていれば、引き金を搾ることもで
きたに違いない。
lines.english: Then he had deliberately approached from behind. Had he truly been carrying a gun, he could surely have pulled the trigger.

lines.japanese:
そのチャンスはいくらでもあったろう。
　無防備の忍の背中を陣取った上で、殺気を向けた
のだ。
lines.english: There would have been plenty of chances. Only once he was in position behind the defenseless Shinobu did he turn his murderous intent on him.

lines.japanese: 「俺もてめぇのことはずっと覚えてたぜ」
lines.english: “I never forgot you either.”
“I see…”

lines.japanese: 「将来を約束されたエリート様だもんな」
lines.english: “You’re an elite with a guaranteed future, after all.”

lines.japanese:
「施設を出たとは聞いてたけど……この街に戻って
　きたのか」
lines.english: “I heard you'd left the institution… So you've come back to this town?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと前にな。まだ荷物も片づいてねぇよ」
lines.english: “A little while back. Haven't even unpacked yet.”

lines.japanese:
親しげな言葉。
　しかし温情など一切込められていない。
lines.english: Friendly words. But they contained not a trace of warmth.

lines.japanese: 「……なんのために？」
lines.english: “…What for?”

lines.japanese:
「仕事だよ。決まってんだろ。俺は満足にガッコに
　も行かせてもらえないんだ。コキ使われて大変な
　んだよ」
lines.english: “Work. What the hell else? They won't even let me attend school properly. They work me like a dog. It's rough.”

lines.japanese:
「すっとぼけてんじゃねぇぞ優等生、てめぇにケチ
　つけられたせいだろうがよ」
lines.english: “Don't play dumb, honor student. This is all because you had to go sticking your nose in.”

lines.japanese:
「ハッ……いや、ただの優等生じゃねぇな。
“汚ねぇ”優等生だな」
lines.english: “Hah… No, you're not just any honor student. You're a dirty honor student.”

lines.japanese: 「同感だ」
lines.english: “I agree.”

lines.japanese:
背中を殴られた。
　肩胛骨間に指の節をねじ込む一撃。
　苦痛に息が止まった。
lines.english: A fist slammed into his back. Knuckles dug between his shoulder blades. The pain stopped his breath.

lines.japanese: 「フカしてんじゃねぇよ」
lines.english: “Don't try to sound tough.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえがここに来るとは思わなかったよ」
lines.english: “I never thought you'd come here.”

lines.japanese:
「俺は真面目だからよ、汚ねぇ優等生野郎がヒヨっ
　てる間に頑張って働きゃあ、こうしてまた会える
　ってわけだ」
lines.english: “See, I'm a hard worker. While a filthy honor-student prick like you chickens out, I work my ass off— and that's how we end up meeting again.”

lines.japanese:
「おまえの道を閉ざしたのは、おまえ自身の行動
　だろ、伊勢崎」
lines.english: “Your own actions closed off your path, didn’t they, Isezaki?”

lines.japanese: 「今はそうやって、冷静に俺の名前を口にしてろよ」
lines.english: “Keep saying my name that calmly while you still can.”

lines.japanese: 「……何をする気だ。また施設に戻りたいのか」
lines.english: “…What are you planning? Do you want to go back to the institution?”

lines.japanese:
「今度はうまくやるさ。
　俺だってちょっとは賢くなったんだ」
lines.english: “I'll get it right this time. I've gotten a little smarter too.”

lines.japanese: 「てめぇのお仲間のことも知ってるぜ」
lines.english: “I know about your little friends.”

lines.japanese: 「ハ、気配変わってんじゃんか。アキレス腱かよ」
lines.english: “Hah. Look at you tense up. Guess that's your Achilles' heel.”

lines.japanese: 「……まさか……おまえ……」
lines.english: “…No… You…”

lines.japanese:
「俺の勉強したところによりますと、アキレス腱っ
　てのは切るためにあるんだよ」
lines.english: “According to my studies, Achilles tendons are made to be cut.”

lines.japanese: 宗多は一人で笑い出した。
lines.english: Souta began laughing to himself.

lines.japanese: 「伊勢崎、宗多……」
lines.english: “Souta Isezaki…”

lines.japanese:
「お、俺の名前まで覚えててくれたのかよ。
　さすが糞優等生野郎だな。記憶力が違うぜ」
lines.english: “Oh, you even remembered my whole name. That's our shitty honor student for you. What a memory.”

lines.japanese:
上機嫌に言ったかと思いきや、一転して低く怒気
を含んだ調子で。
lines.english: One moment he sounded delighted; the next, his voice dropped low with anger.

lines.japanese:
「……そのうち、血を吐くように俺の名前を叫ばせ
　てやっからよ」
lines.english: “…One of these days, I’ll make you scream my name as though you were coughing up blood.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、優等生様は油断しくさっててくださいよ」
lines.english: “Until then, by all means keep your guard down, Mr. Honor Student.”

lines.japanese: 「みんなに手を出すな」
lines.english: “Don't lay a hand on any of them.”

lines.japanese: せいいっぱい凄んで、そう告げる。
lines.english: He put all the menace he could muster behind the words.
“Hah—”

lines.japanese: 宗多が奇声を発した。
lines.english: Souta let out a bizarre cry.

lines.japanese:
いや、違う。
　それは裏返るほどの、哄笑だった。
lines.english: No. Not a cry. It was a roar of laughter so violent his voice cracked.

lines.japanese: 一分。
lines.english: A full minute.

lines.japanese:
「……いや、笑った笑った。確認が取れたぜ。
　一番キクのが何かってな」
lines.english: “…Man, what a laugh. Now I know for sure what hits you hardest.”

lines.japanese:
「おまえみたいな野郎でも、ダチは大事ってか。
　半信半疑だったが……
　ビンゴみたいだな。ＯＫＯＫ」
lines.english: “Even a prick like you cares about his buddies, huh? I wasn't sure, but… Bingo. Okay, okay.”

lines.japanese: 宗多の気配が、すっと離れていく。
lines.english: Souta's presence receded.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあな、優等生」
lines.english: “Later, honor student.”

lines.japanese: 悪意が立ち去っても、忍は動けなかった。
lines.english: Even after that malicious presence withdrew, Shinobu could not move.

lines.japanese:
歯がみする。
　もう少し冷静に対応すべきだった。
　仲間のことは、はぐらかすべきだった。
lines.english: He ground his teeth. He should have handled it more calmly. He should have deflected the subject of his friends.

lines.japanese:
後悔ばかりが胸中に渦巻く。
　どう対応しても、宗多の憎悪を鎮火することは困
難だったろう。
lines.english: Regret churned in his chest. However he had responded, it would probably have been hard to quench Souta’s hatred.

lines.japanese: だとしても思うのだ。
lines.english: Even so, one thought kept returning.

lines.japanese:
軽率だった。
　軽率だった。
　軽率だった。
lines.english: Careless. Careless. Careless.

lines.japanese:
その言葉がぐるぐると回り、なかなか身動きでき
なかった。
lines.english: The word circled endlessly through his mind, and for a long while he could not move.

lines.japanese: 微睡みの中に、忍はいた。
lines.english: Shinobu hovered in a half-doze.

lines.japanese:
ソファに寝ている。
　冷たい空気。
　吸い込むと、鼻孔がシンと痛んだ。
lines.english: He lay on the sofa. Cold air. Each breath left a sharp ache in his nostrils.

lines.japanese: 「え……猟奇事件？」
lines.english: “A… bizarre murder case?”

lines.japanese:
あずさの言葉に、葉子が頷く。
　二人しかいないようだ。
　椅子をつきあわせて、話し込んでいる。
lines.english: Youko nodded at Azusa's question. They seemed to be alone. They had drawn their chairs together and were deep in conversation.

lines.japanese:
背筋を伸ばし、首を落とさずカップを口に運ぶあ
ずさが、奇妙に凛々しい。
lines.english: Azusa looked oddly dignified. She sat straight-backed, lifting the cup to her lips without bowing her head.

lines.japanese:
忍とあずさの二人は猫背で、いつも沙也加に注意
されたものだ。
lines.english: Shinobu and Azusa both tended to slouch, and Sayaka was forever correcting them.

lines.japanese:
それだけ大切な話をしているのか。
　確かに二人の様子には、沈鬱なものが見て取れた。
lines.english: Was their conversation really that serious? There was certainly something somber about them both.

lines.japanese:
身を起こして声をかけたい衝動にかられたが、身
体は石と化したように動かない。
lines.english: He felt the urge to sit up and call to them, but his body would not move, as though it had turned to stone.

lines.japanese:
薄目が拾う狭い情報だけを、漫然と視聴している
だけだった。
lines.english: All he could do was idly watch the narrow slice of the world his half-open eyes admitted.

lines.japanese:
「……実際のところ、犠牲者の数はわからないんで
　すが」
lines.english: “…I don’t actually know how many victims there are.”

lines.japanese:
「でも……その、やっぱり例によって特殊な殺し方、
　なんだよね？」
lines.english: “But… it was that same strange way of killing as before, right?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、このように」
lines.english: “Yes. Like this.”

lines.japanese: 自らの首を、手刀で軽く叩く。
lines.english: She lightly tapped the side of her own neck with the edge of her hand.

lines.japanese: 「バッサリと」
lines.english: “One clean stroke.”

lines.japanese: 「首切り？」
lines.english: “Beheading?”

lines.japanese: 「イエス」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「被害者全員？」
lines.english: “Every victim?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「……死ぬよね」
lines.english: “…That kills you.”

lines.japanese: 「死にますね」
lines.english: “It does.”

lines.japanese:
「……誰か一人がやったことなのかな？
　複数犯とかでなく？」
lines.english: “…Do you think one person did it? Not several people working together?”

lines.japanese:
「犯行に用いられた凶器は、ほぼ同じ形状をした
　刀剣類だそうですよ」
lines.english: “Apparently the murder weapons were blades of almost precisely the same shape.”

lines.japanese:
「ぶっちゃけ刀だってことらしいです。また押さえ
　つけて切断した痕跡もなかったそうな」
lines.english: “Basically, they think it was a katana. And apparently there were no signs that the victims had been held down for the cut.”

lines.japanese:
「信じられないことに、直前まで立っていた人間の
　首を、落とした可能性が高いそうな」
lines.english: “Incredibly, they say it’s highly likely the victims had been standing upright right up until their heads were cut off.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅん。そんなこと、できるんだ」
lines.english: “Huh. I didn't know that was possible.”

lines.japanese: 「んー」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 難しい顔。
lines.english: Youko frowned.

lines.japanese:
「首を落とすというのは、実際のところ難しいんで
　すよ、あずさん」
lines.english: “Actually taking someone's head off is difficult, Azu.”

lines.japanese:
「そうなんだ。まあブシドー経験者のよこさんが言
　うならそうなんだろうけど」
lines.english: “Oh. Well, if Youko, our resident bushido veteran, says so, I'll take her word for it.”

lines.japanese: 「ブシドー経験者にされちゃった……」
lines.english: “Somehow I became a bushido veteran…”

lines.japanese:
「難しいってことは、別の方法で首を切ってるって
　ことかな？」
lines.english: “If it's that difficult, maybe they cut the heads off some other way?”

lines.japanese: 「刀であることは間違いないらしいです。ただ」
lines.english: “It definitely seems to be a sword. But—”

lines.japanese:
「……正直なところ、無理だなって思うです。
　立ってる人間に対する首切り」
lines.english: “…Honestly, I think it's impossible. Beheading someone who's standing up.”

lines.japanese: 「よこさんならできる？」
lines.english: “Could you do it, Youko?”

lines.japanese:
「無理。力も技も足りない。それに頭髪を巻き込ん
　だり、衿があるだけで、かなり変わってきてしま
　う……」
lines.english: “No. I lack both the strength and the technique. Even catching the victim's hair in the stroke, or simply having a collar in the way, makes an enormous difference…”

lines.japanese: 「そか」
lines.english: “Right.”

lines.japanese: 「です」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「つまり、あれだね」
lines.english: “So it's, you know, that.”

lines.japanese: 「あそこです」
lines.english: “Down there.”

lines.japanese: 「今なんかいやらしいニュアンスで言ったぁ」
lines.english: “You just made that sound dirty!”

lines.japanese: 「実際問題いやらしいですから」
lines.english: “The reality is rather dirty.”

lines.japanese: 「いやだよー、そんなよこさんいやだよー」
lines.english: “Nooo! I don't want that kind of Youko!”

lines.japanese: 「事実ですから」
lines.english: “It's true.”

lines.japanese: 「夢見る乙女いじめだ……」
lines.english: “You're bullying a starry-eyed maiden…”

lines.japanese: ポットから紅茶のおかわりを淹れる。
lines.english: She poured herself more tea from the pot.

lines.japanese: 「いる？」
lines.english: “Want some?”

lines.japanese: 「ください」
lines.english: “Please.”

lines.japanese: 「んまいね、これ」
lines.english: “Good stuff, huh?”

lines.japanese: 「よく手に入ったもので」
lines.english: “Amazing we managed to get any.”

lines.japanese: 「沙也加ちんぱわーだね」
lines.english: “Sayaka powerrr.”

lines.japanese: 「金持ってますよ。勝ってます。とこしえに」
lines.english: “She has money. She's winning. Forever.”

lines.japanese: 「にしても、猟奇殺人犯」
lines.english: “Still, though. A bizarre killer.”

lines.japanese: 「今流行の」
lines.english: “The latest fad.”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃまあ……こんな時代だからさ」
lines.english: “Well… look at the times we live in.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、どうやら国もそれは認めたようで」
lines.english: “Apparently even the government has acknowledged it.”

lines.japanese: 「緊急指名手配？」
lines.english: “An emergency manhunt?”

lines.japanese: 「対策チーム、と相成るわけですね」
lines.english: “And thus a task force is born.”

lines.japanese:
「対策チームといっても、数人なんでしょ？
　人手不足だって話だし」
lines.english: “But a ‘task force’ is only a handful of people, right? They're short-staffed as it is.”

lines.japanese: 「殺人鬼が多すぎるですよ」
lines.english: “There are too many murderers, yes.”

lines.japanese: 「そしてスタッフが少なすぎる」
lines.english: “And not nearly enough staff.”

lines.japanese:
「ね、犯人って、やっぱそーとーな達人ってことに
　なるんだよね？」
lines.english: “So the killer must be an incredible expert, right?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 葉子はやりきれない様子で、
lines.english: Looking thoroughly fed up, Youko said—

lines.japanese: 「性豪、と言って良いかと思います」
lines.english: “A master lover, one might say.”

lines.japanese: 「思っちゃだめだそんなこと……」
lines.english: “You're absolutely not allowed to say that…”

lines.japanese: 「それを言うなら剣豪だよ」
lines.english: “The phrase you're looking for is ‘master swordsman.’”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、そのあたりです」
lines.english: “Yes. Somewhere in that vicinity.”

lines.japanese:
「純粋な腕前だけなら、婿殿級を凌駕するかも。
　いや、婿殿はあれでけっこう凄腕だから……」
lines.english: “In pure skill, the killer may even surpass my future husband. Then again, he's quite formidable in his own right…”

lines.japanese: 「婿殿はいいからさ」
lines.english: “Never mind the future husband.”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃふん」
lines.english: “Touché.”

lines.japanese: 「それは言わせたくもないぎゃふんだった……」
lines.english: “That's one ‘touché’ I never wanted to hear…”

lines.japanese:
「剣に命を捧げた人なんて変態なんです。
　変態は常人とは違う価値観でものを見て、そこに
　隠された奥義を引っ張り出すんです」
lines.english: “Anyone who devotes their life to the sword is a pervert. Perverts see the world through values no ordinary person shares, and tease out the secret arts hidden there.”

lines.japanese:
「だから奥義習得のための修行は、しばしば人を
　狂気に追い込む領域で行われる」
lines.english: “That is why training to master a secret art so often takes place in realms that drive people mad.”

lines.japanese: 「狂ってるから、見えるルール……」
lines.english: “Rules that only madness lets you see…”

lines.japanese: 「何か気になることでも？」
lines.english: “Is something bothering you?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん……今となってはなんだけどさ」
lines.english: “No… It's a little late to wonder now, but—”

lines.japanese:
「首切り犯が凄い技術を持っている。その力で人を
　殺している」
lines.english: “The killer has this incredible skill, and they're using it to kill people.”

lines.japanese: 「本当にただそれだけのことなのかなって思って」
lines.english: “I just wondered if that was really all there was to it.”

lines.japanese:
「被害者に統一性はないみたい。もしかしたらある
　のかも知れないけど……私たちには見分けのつか
　ない、独自の規則が」
lines.english: “There seems to be no common thread among the victims. Maybe there is one, but… some private rule we can’t discern.”

lines.japanese:
「うん……考えても仕方ないことなんだけどさ。
　ごめんね、突然変なこと言った」
lines.english: “Yeah… There's no point thinking about it, though. Sorry. That was a strange thing to say out of nowhere.”

lines.japanese: 「続けて。聞きます」
lines.english: “Go on. I'm listening.”

lines.japanese:
「凄い首切り殺法でたくさん殺す。
　だから猟奇殺人犯」
lines.english: “They use an incredible beheading technique to kill lots of people. That's what makes them a bizarre killer.”

lines.japanese:
「なんで殺すか普通の人にはわからない。
　分析しないとわからない。だから猟奇殺人犯」
lines.english: “Ordinary people can't understand why. It takes analysis to understand. That's what makes them a bizarre killer.”

lines.japanese:
「殺した人たちを恨んでいたわけじゃない。
　殺したいって思っているとも限らない」
lines.english: “They didn't hate the people they killed. They might not even have wanted to kill them.”

lines.japanese:
「……殺さないといけない理由があるから、殺すん
　だよね？」
lines.english: “…They kill because there's some reason they have to kill, right?”

lines.japanese:
「今回は性的暴行のあとがないそうなので、
　そういう線はのぞくとして」
lines.english: “Apparently there were no signs of sexual assault this time, so setting that possibility aside—”

lines.japanese: 「にゃむ」
lines.english: “Mrrm.”

lines.japanese: 「恨みの線、これもないような気がする」
lines.english: “I don't think it was a grudge either.”

lines.japanese:
「そうなの？　地に足のついた恨みでなくても、
　たとえば本人ルールでさ、短髪の人間が憎いとか
　あるかもよ？」
lines.english: “You don't think so? It doesn't have to be a reasonable grudge. Maybe the killer has some private rule, like hating everyone with short hair.”

lines.japanese: 「だって、殺し方が優しい」
lines.english: “Because it's a gentle way to kill.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
少し唖然とする。
　当然の反応であったはずだ。
　葉子は真面目に応じる。
lines.english: Azusa stared, briefly at a loss. Surely a natural enough response. Youko answered with complete seriousness.

lines.japanese: 「斬首は、優しい」
lines.english: “Decapitation is gentle.”

lines.japanese: 噛み含めるよう、言った。
lines.english: She spoke slowly and carefully.

lines.japanese:
「憎悪があるなら、もっと苦痛のある殺し方をする
　と思う」
lines.english: “If hatred were involved, I think the killer would choose a more painful method.”

lines.japanese: 「確かに即死、だよね。首切りは」
lines.english: “I guess it does kill you instantly. Beheading, I mean.”

lines.japanese: 「ほぼ即死、と言われてますね」
lines.english: “It's said to be almost instantaneous.”

lines.japanese: 「……ふぉ、ふぉぼ？　え、なにそれ？」
lines.english: “…N-Nearly? Wait, what does that mean?”

lines.japanese: 「短時間、意識が残っているという説が」
lines.english: “There's a theory that consciousness lingers briefly.”
“……Yikes.”

lines.japanese:
「この一点だけで憎悪説はないと思ってもいいかな
　ーと素人だから思いますよ」
lines.english: “Speaking purely as an amateur, I think this one detail may be enough to rule out hatred as the motive.”

lines.japanese:
「もちろん犯人に、連続殺人をすることによる経済
　的恩恵はない」
lines.english: “And of course, the killer gains no financial benefit from these serial murders.”

lines.japanese:
「性的なものでもなく、憎悪でもなく、経済的意味
　がなく、突発的なものでもなく、かといって厳密
　な意味で計画性があるものではない」
lines.english: “It isn't sexual, driven by hatred, or profitable. It isn't spontaneous, yet neither is it planned in the strictest sense.”

lines.japanese:
「まるで、やらねばならないことを、淡々と実行し
　ているような……そんな感じですね」
lines.english: “It feels as if the killer is calmly carrying out something that simply has to be done…”

lines.japanese: 「やらねばならないこと……」
lines.english: “A necessary task…”

lines.japanese:
「妄想から分岐した、ある種の儀式か、義務感とい
　う説が濃厚のような」
lines.english: “The leading theory seems to be some kind of ritual or sense of duty stemming from a delusion.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、あたしもそう思うな」
lines.english: “Yeah. That's what I think too.”

lines.japanese:
「理由はいろいろあるんだろうけど、
　本人にしかわからないから、周囲から見て猟奇
　なんだろうね……」
lines.english: “There could be all kinds of reasons, but only the killer understands them. I guess that's why it seems so bizarre to everyone else…”

lines.japanese:
「そういう妄想というか、狂った部分って、結構まと
　もなところから生えてるような気がするよ」
lines.english: “I feel like those delusions—those crazy parts of people— often sprout from somewhere pretty ordinary.”

lines.japanese:
「何のためか、となると、より細かな分析を待つし
　かないわけです」
lines.english: “We'll have to wait for a more detailed analysis before we can say what purpose it serves.”

lines.japanese: 「だよねぇ」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
「さっきの斬首の話なんですけど……
　あれ、介錯だと思うんです」
lines.english: “About those decapitations earlier… I think they're kaishaku.”

lines.japanese: 「カイシャク？」
lines.english: “Kai-sha-ku?”

lines.japanese: 「サムライの、介錯です」
lines.english: “Samurai kaishaku.”

lines.japanese: 「ええと、つまり打ち首とか切腹の？」
lines.english: “You mean the kind used for execution by beheading, or for seppuku?”

lines.japanese: 「はい。慈悲の心、武士の情けってやつで」
lines.english: “Yes. An act of mercy. A warrior's compassion.”

lines.japanese: 「残酷なのに？」
lines.english: “Even though it's so brutal?”

lines.japanese:
「苦痛を与える殺し方は見苦しいんでしょう。
　だって武士だから」
lines.english: “A way of killing that causes suffering must strike them as unseemly. They are warriors, after all.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そっか……」
lines.english: “Oh. Right…”

lines.japanese: 「だから、斬首である必要があるんですよ」
lines.english: “That's why it has to be decapitation.”

lines.japanese: 「斬首は、武士ですよね」
lines.english: “Beheading is the warrior's way, isn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「そだね」
lines.english: “I guess so.”

lines.japanese:
「刀に長けた者……武士にとって、困難かつ即死を
　もたらす慈悲の技……この意味は大きいですよ」
lines.english: “For one skilled with the sword… for a warrior, it is a difficult but merciful technique that brings instant death… That distinction matters a great deal.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese:
「だとするなら、結構簡単な構図です。殺人犯は、
　狂っているなりにロジックに乗っ取って行動して
　いるわけです」
lines.english: “If so, the picture is fairly simple. Mad though the murderer may be, their actions follow a logic of their own.”

lines.japanese: 「現代に甦った正義の武士というわけですね」
lines.english: “A righteous warrior reborn in the modern age.”

lines.japanese: 「……正義じゃないよぅ」
lines.english: “…There's nothing righteous about it.”

lines.japanese:
「でも介錯？
　本人は救っているつもりだってこと？」
lines.english: “But kaishaku? The killer thinks they're saving people?”

lines.japanese: 「あくまで可能性として」
lines.english: “It's only one possibility.”

lines.japanese: 「それだといろいろ説明がつくんです」
lines.english: “It would explain a great deal.”

lines.japanese: 「性も憎悪も経済も合理もないことの説明が」
lines.english: “It would explain why sex, hatred, profit, and rational motive are all absent.”

lines.japanese: 「それで正義って言ったんだ」
lines.english: “That's why you called it righteous.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ優しく、殺すのは……」
lines.english: “Then the reason they kill so gently…”

lines.japanese: 「救いだから」
lines.english: “Is because it's salvation.”
“…Kaishaku.”

lines.japanese:
「正確には切腹における介錯人というのは、
　まあお手伝い要員なんですけどね」
lines.english: “Strictly speaking, the kaishakunin in a seppuku ceremony is more of an assistant, though.”

lines.japanese:
「首を落とすときに抱き首という形を作る都合で、
　背中側から斬るんですけど」
lines.english: “To produce what is called a ‘cradled head,’ the kaishakunin cuts from behind.”

lines.japanese: 「この犯人、真正面から斬ってるそうで」
lines.english: “But apparently this killer strikes from directly in front.”

lines.japanese: 「………ええと、抱き首ってのは？」
lines.english: “…Um, what exactly is a ‘cradled head’?”

lines.japanese:
「つまり、地面に頭を落とすのは卑賤な殺し方。
　皮を残して、切腹した人間の膝元に首を抱かせる
　ようにするのは、武士に相応しい死に方」
lines.english: “Letting a head fall to the ground is considered a lowly death. So they leave a strip of skin at the front intact, letting the head hang into the lap of the one performing seppuku—a death befitting a warrior.”

lines.japanese: 「その考え方も……どこかおかしいね」
lines.english: “That way of thinking… is strange too.”

lines.japanese:
「つい最近まで、世界はおかしかったんですよ。
　ううん、今もまんべんなくおかしい。
　ほんの十年前、二十年前もおかしい。そもそも」
lines.english: “The world was strange until very recently. No—it's strange through and through even now. It was strange ten years ago and twenty years ago. To begin with—”

lines.japanese: じっとあずさを見つめる。
lines.english: She stared intently at Azusa.

lines.japanese:
「世界がまともでいた瞬間が、人が地に満ちて以降、
　果たして一秒たりとてあったのかどうか―――」
lines.english: “Since humanity filled the earth, has there ever been even a single second when the world was sane—?”

lines.japanese:
あずさはばつの悪そうな顔を浮かべた。
　思うところがあったのだろう。
lines.english: Azusa looked uncomfortable. She must have had something on her mind.

lines.japanese:
「……もし、犯人が世のため人のためにそれを成し
　遂げないといけないって信じているなら……悲し
　いね」
lines.english: “…If the killer believes they have to accomplish this for the good of the world and everyone in it… then that's sad.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese:
「本人は正しいと信じているのに、それは間違いで、
　残酷なことで」
lines.english: “They believe they're right, but they're wrong, and what they do is cruel.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、そんなことはよくあるじゃないですか」
lines.english: “But doesn't that happen all the time?”

lines.japanese:
「日々の生活の中でも、ささいな行き違いはいくら
　でもある」
lines.english: “Even in ordinary life, there are countless little ways people misunderstand one another.”

lines.japanese:
「被害がなければ、性格のすれ違いで済んでしまう
　ことですけどね」
lines.english: “When no one is hurt, we dismiss it as a clash of personalities.”

lines.japanese: 「個性も“狂い”には違いないわけで」
lines.english: “Individuality itself is a kind of ‘madness.’”

lines.japanese:
「でもさ、道を間違えなければ……その人は正しい
　力の使い方ができたのかも知れないのに」
lines.english: “But if they hadn't taken the wrong path… maybe they could have used their strength the right way.”

lines.japanese: 「あずさん」
lines.english: “Azu.”

lines.japanese: あずさの瞳に潜水するように顔を寄せる。
lines.english: She leaned close, as though diving into Azusa's eyes.

lines.japanese: 「な、なに？」
lines.english: “W-What?”

lines.japanese: 少しのけぞるあずさ。
lines.english: Azusa leaned back a little.

lines.japanese: 「悪行は罪です。自覚ある悪行は潔いですが罪です」
lines.english: “An evil deed is a sin. Evil done knowingly may at least be honest, but it is still sin.”

lines.japanese: 「しかしもっとも危険なのは、自覚のない善行です」
lines.english: “But most dangerous of all is a good deed done blindly.”

lines.japanese: 「それは、どうして？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese:
「革命の論理ですから……自分のしている行為がど
　のような結果を招き、誰をどれだけ傷つけようと
　も、欺瞞による自己正当化が起こります」
lines.english: “Because that is the logic of revolution… No matter what consequences your actions bring, whom they hurt or how badly, self-deception lets you justify yourself.”

lines.japanese:
「正しいからやってよい。
　その感覚を持ってしまうと、どんな残酷なことも
　できてしまいます」
lines.english: “It is right, therefore I may do it. Once you come to feel that way, you can commit any atrocity.”

lines.japanese:
「でもそれは本当ならば、罪の苛烈さをともなう茨
　の道」
lines.english: “But in truth, that is a thorny road, carrying the terrible weight of sin.”

lines.japanese: 「心の痛みを代償に支払い続ける必要があるんです」
lines.english: “You have to go on paying for it with the pain in your own heart.”

lines.japanese:
「背負えるだけの罪より大きく、人を救おうとする
　のは危険なんです」
lines.english: “Trying to save people by taking on more sin than you can carry is dangerous.”

lines.japanese: 「善意であっても」
lines.english: “Even with good intentions?”

lines.japanese: 「善意であるからこそ」
lines.english: “Precisely because the intentions are good.”

lines.japanese: 「もし、世界中の罪を背負えたら？」
lines.english: “What if someone could carry all the world's sins?”

lines.japanese: 「……その人は、壊れていくでしょうね」
lines.english: “…I imagine they would break.”

lines.japanese: 「難しい。よこさん」
lines.english: “That's a hard one, Youko.”

lines.japanese:
「言ってる私も理解してないです。
　聞きかじってます」
lines.english: “I don't understand it myself. I'm only repeating something I heard secondhand.”

lines.japanese: 「だめじゃん」
lines.english: “Well, that's no good.”

lines.japanese: あずさはすっかり冷えた紅茶に、乾いた唇を浸す。
lines.english: Azusa pressed her dry lips to tea that had gone completely cold.

lines.japanese: 「なんにせよ、いい人には壊れないで欲しいな」
lines.english: “Whatever happens, I don't want good people to break.”

lines.japanese: 「……こんな時代ですから、難しいですよ」
lines.english: “…In times like these, that is difficult.”

lines.japanese: 「７面ボス戦くらいに難しいんです」
lines.english: “As difficult as a stage-seven boss.”

lines.japanese: 「ものによるよね……」
lines.english: “Depends on the game…”

lines.japanese:
「シューティング・ブレードでボス瞬殺するような
　あずさんにはわからないんです……」
lines.english: “Azu, you wipe bosses out in seconds with the Shooting Blade. You wouldn't understand…”

hyperlinks.preview: A shooting game. A game where you get shot.

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: A shooting game. A game where you get shot.

lines.japanese:
「だってさっさと倒さないとよこさん機、弾に当た
　りに行くんだもん」
lines.english: “Because if I don't beat them quickly, you fly your ship straight into the bullets!”

lines.japanese: 「よけてるつもりなのに……」
lines.english: “I'm trying to dodge them…”

lines.japanese: 「下の方で誘導弾だけ撃ってくれればいいんだよ」
lines.english: “All you have to do is stay low and fire homing shots.”

lines.japanese: 「……存在意義を、感じたい」
lines.english: “…I want to feel that my existence has meaning.”

lines.japanese: 「でもちょっとひっかかるな」
lines.english: “Something still bothers me, though.”

lines.japanese: 「はい？」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese: 「優しい猟奇殺人」
lines.english: “A bizarre murder carried out gently.”

lines.japanese: 「これ自体、ただの仮説ですから」
lines.english: “The idea itself is only a hypothesis.”

lines.japanese:
「いや……もしかすると、殺す対象より殺し方なの
　かもって思って」
lines.english: “No… I wondered if the way the killer does it matters more than who they kill.”

lines.japanese: 「と言いますと？」
lines.english: “Meaning?”

lines.japanese:
「首を切断する……と、確実に殺せる、から……
　うーん」
lines.english: “Cutting off the head… makes absolutely sure they're dead, so… hmm.”

lines.japanese: 「だから……つまり……」
lines.english: “So… what I mean is…”

lines.japanese: 「つまり？」
lines.english: “Meaning?”

lines.japanese: 「うーむーん」
lines.english: “Hmmm-mmm.”

lines.japanese:
あずさは顔をあげた。
　苦笑い。
lines.english: Azusa looked up. She smiled wryly.

lines.japanese: 「わかんなー」
lines.english: “Dunno!”

lines.japanese: 「安楽椅子探偵失格とさせていただきます」
lines.english: “Then I must disqualify you as an armchair detective.”

lines.japanese: 葉子はお辞儀をする。
lines.english: Youko bowed.

lines.japanese: 「いやいやいやいや、もともと素人だし」
lines.english: “No, no, no, no—I was an amateur from the start.”

lines.japanese:
「……ちなみに首切りって、よこさんでも無理なん
　だよね？」
lines.english: “…By the way, even you couldn't behead someone, right?”

lines.japanese: 「とても難しいかと」
lines.english: “I think it would be extremely difficult.”

lines.japanese: 「……お兄さんだったら？」
lines.english: “…What about your brother?”

lines.japanese: 「兄だったら」
lines.english: “If it were my brother—”

lines.japanese:
双眼が鋭く絞られる。
　何かを懸念するように。
lines.english: Her eyes narrowed sharply. Something seemed to trouble her.

lines.japanese: 「できる、かも知れません」
lines.english: “He might be able to.”

lines.japanese: 「強いんだ。見たことない」
lines.english: “He's that strong? I've never seen him fight.”

lines.japanese: 「見たらエロいって思う」
lines.english: “If you did, you'd think it was sexy.”

lines.japanese: 「エロいのか……どんな強さなんだ……」
lines.english: “Sexy, huh… What kind of strength is that…?”

lines.japanese: 「太刀筋が、こう、マンガみたいな」
lines.english: “The way his blade moves is, well, straight out of a manga.”

lines.japanese: 「ザシューっと？」
lines.english: “Like, shhhnk?”

lines.japanese: 「どっちかというとズバッシャー」
lines.english: “More like zwasshh.”

lines.japanese: 「すっげぇ見たぁ」
lines.english: “I seriously wanna see that.”

lines.japanese: 少女たちの、華やかな会話を遠くに見る。
lines.english: He watched the girls' animated conversation from a distance.

lines.japanese:
その輪の中に、入ることができない気がした。
　ただ見ているだけ。
lines.english: He felt that he could not join their circle. He could only watch.

lines.japanese:
涙は瞳を厚く多い、視覚情報を劣化させる。
　ぼけた世界は、童話のそれとなんら変わりはない。
lines.english: Tears covered his eyes in a thick film, degrading the image. The blurred world was no different from a fairy tale.

lines.japanese:
なぜ体がうまく動かないのか。
　寝ぼけているせいだ、体調が悪いせいだ、と理解
することは難しかった。
lines.english: Why wouldn’t his body do what he wanted? It was hard to put it down to drowsiness or poor health.

lines.japanese: 無量の哀感が、心を焦がすままにさせてしまう。
lines.english: Immeasurable sorrow burned unchecked in his heart.

lines.japanese: 「……あ、忍くん、起きた」
lines.english: “…Oh. Shinobu's awake.”

lines.japanese:
あずさが立ち上がって、こちらにやってくる。
　視界の中、癖毛の少女が占める領域は、どんどん
大きくなっていく。
lines.english: Azusa rose and came toward him. Within his field of vision, the tousle-haired girl took up more and more space.

lines.japanese: いっぱいに、
lines.english: Until she filled it—

lines.japanese: 「……頭痛、もう平気？　熱とか、どうかな―――」
lines.english: “…Is your headache better? How's your fever—?”

lines.japanese:
優しい声。
　真綿のようなてのひら。
　額に触れた。
lines.english: A gentle voice. A palm soft as spun silk. It touched his forehead.

lines.japanese:
満たすものと吹き抜けるものが心に同居して、咀
嚼できない感情となってしこる。
　貴宮忍の目と意識は、閉ざされた。
lines.english: What filled his heart and what swept through it lingered there together, congealing into an emotion he could not digest. Shinobu Atemiya's eyes closed, and his consciousness with them.

lines.japanese: 学校で寝ていた。
lines.english: He had fallen asleep at school.

lines.japanese: （いかん……何してるんだ……）
lines.english: (This isn't good… What am I doing…?)

lines.japanese:
長時間机に突っ伏していたようだ。
　節々が軽く痛んだ。
　教室には誰もいなかった。
lines.english: He seemed to have spent a long time facedown on his desk. His joints ached faintly. The classroom was empty.

lines.japanese: 当然であろう。
lines.english: Naturally.

lines.japanese:
窓の外を見やる。
　多分に時間を無駄にしたであろうことが、空の色
からよく理解できる。
lines.english: He looked out the window. The color of the sky made it clear that he must have wasted a good deal of time.

lines.japanese: 茜色。夕刻だ。
lines.english: Crimson. Evening.

lines.japanese:
空気に透ける淡紅色。
　不純物のない平坦な色合い。
lines.english: Pale crimson, transparent in the air. A flat, unblemished wash of color.

lines.japanese:
どこか寂しくもあるが、安心できた。
　かきたてるような不安もそこにはない。
　であるならば、忍が黄昏を嫌う理由はない。
lines.english: Somehow lonely, but comforting. There was nothing there to unsettle him. And so Shinobu had no reason to dislike the twilight.

lines.japanese:
老年の日のように枯れてはいるが、穏やかで、揺
らぐことがない。
lines.english: It had the faded quality of a day in old age, yet it was gentle and unwavering.

lines.japanese: 希望がないなら、止められるものは安寧だけである。
lines.english: With no hope left, only peace could still him.

lines.japanese: （……空……高いや）
lines.english: (…The sky… it's so high.)

lines.japanese:
窓際に寄った。
　空には雲が薄くかかっていた。
　その高さは、どこまでも遠く高い。
lines.english: He went to the window. A thin veil of cloud hung in the sky. That height stretched endlessly away.

lines.japanese:
かつて、忍は空を恐れていたことがある。
　見ていると、不確かな高度を感じ取ることができ
ず、意識を吸い取られてしまいそうになった。
lines.english: Once, Shinobu had been afraid of the sky. Looking at it, unable to grasp its uncertain height, he would feel it drinking away his consciousness.

lines.japanese:
雲が低く降りている時には、逆に押し潰されそう
な不安があった。
lines.english: When the clouds hung low, by contrast, he had feared they would crush him.

lines.japanese:
空は見当識を狂わせるものだった。
　だが今は……さほどのこともない。
lines.english: The sky used to rob him of his bearings. But now… it hardly mattered.

lines.japanese: （どうしてかな、穏やかな気分だ―――）
lines.english: (I wonder why I feel so calm—)

lines.japanese: 背後、扉が開く音。
lines.english: Behind him, the sound of the door opening.

lines.japanese: 「……もしもしー？」
lines.english: “…Hellooo?”

lines.japanese: 葉子だった。
lines.english: It was Youko.

lines.japanese: 「忍さんめっけ」
lines.english: “Found you, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese:
「教室に一人、世界の中心に忘れ去られて叫んだり
　する感じで佇む忍さんを発見」
lines.english: “I found Shinobu alone in a classroom, standing there forgotten at the center of the world as though he were about to cry out.”

lines.japanese: 「現代を映すような鋭い感性」
lines.english: “A keen sensibility that holds a mirror to modernity.”

lines.japanese: 「……失礼しまーす」
lines.english: “…Pardon the intrusion.”

lines.japanese:
教室に入ってくる。
　上級生の教室に入る際のためらいが、葉子の姿勢
を少し低くする。
lines.english: She came into the room. Hesitant about entering an upperclassman’s classroom, Youko held herself a little lower.

lines.japanese: 「今日は私でした」
lines.english: “It was my turn today.”
(…What was?)

lines.japanese: 腕を取る。
lines.english: She took his arm.

lines.japanese: 「ということで、帰りましょう」
lines.english: “So, let's go home.”

lines.japanese: 「それとも、用事でも？」
lines.english: “Or did you have plans?”

lines.japanese: ありはしない。
lines.english: He had none.

lines.japanese: 「……ずっと寝てた」
lines.english: “…I slept this whole time.”

lines.japanese: 「そうですか」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「眠くて」
lines.english: “I was sleepy.”
“Tears.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 葉子の指が、さらりと目尻に押し当てられた。
lines.english: Youko's finger came lightly to rest at the corner of his eye.

lines.japanese: 「……悲しい、夢？」
lines.english: “…A sad dream?”

lines.japanese: 「どうだろう」
lines.english: “I'm not sure.”

lines.japanese: よく記憶できていない。
lines.english: He did not remember it well.

lines.japanese: 「時間、無駄にしたかな」
lines.english: “Did I waste all that time?”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことありません」
lines.english: “Not at all.”

lines.japanese: 「意味のある時間ですよ」
lines.english: “It had meaning.”

lines.japanese: 「どんな？」
lines.english: “How so?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ？」
lines.english: “Who knows?”

lines.japanese:
しかし葉子は、含みのある笑みを忍に向ける。
　教えてはくれないらしい。
lines.english: Yet Youko gave him a knowing smile. Apparently she did not intend to tell him.

lines.japanese:
その顔から、風船から空気がこぼれる速度で、笑
みが抜けていった。
lines.english: Her smile leaked away like air from a balloon.

lines.japanese: 「泣いたらだめです」
lines.english: “You mustn't cry.”

lines.japanese: と言う。
lines.english: So she said.

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Mm.”

lines.japanese: 「忍さんは泣かなくてもいいんです」
lines.english: “You don't need to cry, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese:
理由は理解できなかった。
　ただ、ありがたいと感じた。
lines.english: He did not understand why. He was simply grateful.

lines.japanese:
それでも“良かった”とは思えない。
　心にタールがこびりついたようだ。落ちない。
　その発する悪臭が、忍の涙腺を絞ろうとするのか。
lines.english: Even so, he couldn't bring himself to think, “That's good.” It was as though tar clung to his heart and would not come off. Was its stench trying to wring tears from his eyes?

lines.japanese: 痛みが、頭の芯に響いた。おなじみ偏頭痛だ。
lines.english: Pain rang through the core of his head. His old familiar migraine.

lines.japanese:
過ぎた頭痛は、眩暈を引き起こす。
　今がそうだった。
lines.english: A bad enough headache brought vertigo with it. This one was no exception.
“Oh, not again…”

lines.japanese:
鞄の中から、乙女袋を取り出す。
　ここ一年、葉子はいつも携帯しているものだ。
lines.english: She took the maiden's pouch from her bag. Youko had carried it everywhere for the past year.

lines.japanese: 「頭痛薬、わけてあげますね」
lines.english: “I'll give you some headache medicine.”

lines.japanese:
最初に取り出したのは、粉薬だった。
　パケを破り、水もなしに忍の口に流し込もうとする。
lines.english: First she produced a packet of powder. She tore it open and tried to pour the powder into Shinobu's mouth without water.

lines.japanese: 「うっ、うぷっ！」
lines.english: “Mmph—guh!”

lines.japanese: 全然ダメだった。
lines.english: A complete failure.

lines.japanese: 死ぬほど不器用だ。
lines.english: Her clumsiness was lethal.

lines.japanese: 「けほっ、けほっ！」
lines.english: “Cough, cough!”

lines.japanese:
仕方なく、もっと服用しやすいカプセル型の市販
薬を取り出す。
lines.english: With no other choice, she took out an over-the-counter capsule that would be easier to swallow.

lines.japanese:
粉薬に比べて、効き目は鈍い。
　だが何も服用しないよりはましだ。
lines.english: It was less effective than the powder. But it was better than taking nothing.

lines.japanese: 「忍さん、これこれ」
lines.english: “Here, Shinobu. This one.”

lines.japanese:
カプセルを口内に入れようとするが、間違えてス
ムーズに鼻の穴に入れてしまう葉子だ。
lines.english: She tried to put the capsule into his mouth and instead slid it smoothly into his nostril.

lines.japanese: 「……げほっ、がほっ！」
lines.english: “…Geh—gah!”

lines.japanese:
鼻孔の奥、指では取り出せないため、除去のため
に忍は大変な苦労をした。
lines.english: It was too deep in his nostril to reach with a finger, and Shinobu had a terrible time getting it out.

lines.japanese: 「むう、いけません」
lines.english: “Hmm. No, this won't do.”

lines.japanese:
葉子はカプセルを口に放り込んだ。自分の。
　そしてキス。ディープ。
lines.english: Youko tossed a capsule into a mouth. Her own. Then came a kiss. A deep one.

lines.japanese: 「んんんんんんん！？」
lines.english: “Mmmmmmmmm!?”

lines.japanese: ちゅぽん、と音を立てて葉子は離れた。
lines.english: Youko drew away with a wet pop.

lines.japanese:
忍は机に伏して、小さく肩を震わせた。
　そんな忍を、高い位置から傲然と見下ろして、
葉子は言った。
lines.english: Shinobu slumped over his desk, his shoulders trembling faintly. Youko stood over him imperiously and said—

lines.japanese: 「帰りますか？　まだいますか？」
lines.english: “Are we going home? Or are you staying here?”

lines.japanese: 「うう……奪われた……」
lines.english: “Ugh… I've been robbed…”

lines.japanese:
「遅くなると物騒ですから、はやく帰った方がいい
　気がしますけど」
lines.english: “It’s dangerous to be out late. I think you should go home soon.”

lines.japanese: 「……そう……だね」
lines.english: “…You're… right.”

lines.japanese: ぼんやりと答える。
lines.english: He answered in a daze.

lines.japanese: （帰る……帰るのか？）
lines.english: (Home… Am I going home?)

lines.japanese:
どこかに物足りない気持ちがある。
　が、ざっと考えを巡らせてみても答えが見つから
ない。
lines.english: Something still felt missing. But even after turning it over in his mind, he found no answer.

lines.japanese: 嫌になってしまった。
lines.english: He was sick of it.

lines.japanese: 「帰ろう」
lines.english: “Let's go.”

lines.japanese: 「はいー」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: ぐい、と絡められた腕を引かれる。
lines.english: She tugged hard on his arm, still linked with hers.

lines.japanese: 忍の片足が床を離れた。
lines.english: One of Shinobu's feet left the floor.

lines.japanese: 葉子はぐいぐいと忍を引いていく。
lines.english: Youko hauled Shinobu along.

lines.japanese:
長い放課後。
　人気はない。
lines.english: The after-school hours stretched on. Not a soul around.

lines.japanese: 「頭痛、平気でしょうか？」
lines.english: “Is your headache okay?”

lines.japanese: 「……ん？　うん、最近はたいしたことない」
lines.english: “…Hm? Yeah. It hasn't been too bad lately.”

lines.japanese: 「頭痛持ちだってことも忘れてたくらいだよ」
lines.english: “I'd practically forgotten I was prone to them.”

lines.japanese: 「ズツートレチャウーノ」
lines.english: “Headache-Be-Gone.”

lines.japanese: 「が効いているんですかね」
lines.english: “Do you suppose it's working?”

lines.english: “You really like that medicine, don't you?”

lines.japanese: 「自分では飲まないのに買っちゃうんですよ」
lines.english: “I keep buying it even though I never take any myself.”

lines.japanese: 「そう」

lines.japanese:
「あまり痛くはないんですけど、重くて量も多いん

lines.japanese: 「恥じらいを、持って」
lines.english: “Have some shame.”

lines.japanese: 「勉強中です」
lines.english: “I'm working on it.”

lines.japanese: 「頑張って」
lines.english: “Keep at it.”

lines.japanese: 「はやく人間になりたい」
lines.english: “I want to be human already.”

lines.japanese: 「人だよ、もう立派な」
lines.english: “You already are—a perfectly fine human being.”

lines.japanese: 「本当ですか？」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese: 「すごくヘンだけど」

lines.japanese: 「……うーん」
lines.english: “…Hmm.”

lines.japanese:
廊下の柱に穿たれた大きな疵痕を見ながら、忍と

lines.english: Looking at the deep scars gouged into the corridor pillars, Shinobu and Youko tottered toward the entrance.

lines.japanese:
賑わう商店街を抜けていく。

lines.english: They made their way through the bustling shopping district. The evening sun slanting through the arcade roof lent the tunnel-like space a peculiar beauty.

lines.japanese: 葉子が天井を見た。
lines.english: Youko looked up at the ceiling.

lines.japanese: 「……今日もバリヤー張ってないです」
lines.english: “…The barrier isn't up today either.”

lines.japanese:
「バリヤーって……ああ、もしかして天井カバーの
　こと？」
lines.english: “Barrier…? Oh, do you mean the roof cover?”

lines.japanese:
アーケードの外側には、雹などの被害から守るた
めの金属製スライド・カバーが備え付けられている。
lines.english: The outside of the arcade was fitted with a sliding metal cover designed to protect it from hail and similar damage.

lines.japanese:
もちろん人力で動かせるわけもなく、モーターに
よって開閉される。
lines.english: Naturally, it could not be moved by hand; motors opened and closed it.

lines.japanese:
忍も葉子も、存在は知っていたが見たことはなか
った。
lines.english: Both Shinobu and Youko knew it existed, but neither had ever seen it.

lines.japanese: 「みたい」
lines.english: “I want to see it.”

lines.japanese:
「……雹とか豪雨の時は閉めるって聞いたけど。
　さすがにそうそうあるものじゃないよ」
lines.english: “…I hear they close it during hailstorms or torrential rain, but those don't happen very often.”

lines.english: “Shall we attack it?”

lines.japanese: 「……どうやって」
lines.english: “…How?”

lines.japanese: 「閉まるかも」
lines.english: “It might close.”

lines.japanese: 「防御力高そうだよ」
lines.english: “Its defense looks pretty high.”

lines.japanese: 会話が斜め方向に滑り落ちていく。
lines.english: The conversation went skidding off at an angle.

lines.japanese: 「光線では―――」
lines.english: “With a beam—”

lines.japanese: 「メーサー砲とか―――」
lines.english: “A maser cannon, perhaps—”

lines.japanese: 「メガ粒子砲―――」
lines.english: “A mega-particle cannon—”

lines.japanese: 「電磁制御の巨大ヨーヨーで―――」
lines.english: “An enormous electromagnetically controlled yo-yo—”

lines.japanese: 「クローあたりが好みで―――」
lines.english: “I think I'd prefer a claw—”

lines.japanese: 「コンピューター制御されたカマで―――」
lines.english: “A computer-controlled sickle—”

lines.japanese: 「バールのようなもの―――」
lines.english: “Something resembling a crowbar—”

lines.japanese: 「ドリル戦車が―――」
lines.english: “A drill tank—”

lines.japanese:
適切なコメントを挟む者がいないと、どこまでも
ねじ曲がっていくものだ。
lines.english: Without anyone to cut in with the right comment, a conversation could keep twisting forever.

lines.japanese:
「そういえばツイン・ドリルの髪型というのがあっ
　て」
lines.english: “Speaking of drills, there's a hairstyle called twin drills.”

lines.japanese: 「似合うと思うよ」
lines.english: “I think it would suit you.”

lines.japanese: 「たてまきロール……」
lines.english: “Vertical ringlets…”

lines.japanese: 「長さがちょっと足りないかな？」
lines.english: “Your hair may be a little too short.”

lines.japanese: 「伸ばしましょうか？」
lines.english: “Should I grow it out?”

lines.japanese: 「ドリルにするために？」
lines.english: “For the drills?”

lines.japanese: 「ツイン・テールよりは強いと思うんですが」
lines.english: “I think they'd be stronger than twin tails.”

lines.japanese: 「攻撃力では勝っていそうだけど」
lines.english: “Their attack power does look higher.”

lines.japanese:
「一応、仲間うちでの重複がないように気をつける
　と、ただのロングにはしにくいわけで」
lines.english: “If I’m trying not to match anyone else in our group, plain long hair is a difficult choice.”

lines.japanese: 「沙也加がいるね」
lines.english: “There's Sayaka.”

lines.japanese:
「あずささんもショートなんで、ちょっと気になり
　ます」
lines.english: “Azusa has short hair too, which bothers me a little.”

lines.japanese:
「葉子とは印象違うけどね。
　制服が違うせいもあるのかな」
lines.english: “She gives a different impression than you. Maybe it's partly the different uniforms.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 「ロングまで伸ばして……何か斬新な髪型に―――」
lines.english: “I'll grow it long… and then do something original with it—”

lines.japanese:
ハッ、と何か思いつく葉子。
