かつて忍は六度、求めた。
　そして六度、手に入れた。
lines.english: Six times before, Shinobu had gone after what he wanted. Six times, he had won it.

lines.japanese:
今度は維持しなければならない。
　六度だけではない。
lines.english: This time, he had to hold on to what he had won. And six times would not be enough.

lines.japanese:
危機に陥るならば、何度でも、守っていかねば
ならない。何度でも。
lines.english: Whenever it fell into danger, he would have to protect it again and again. As many times as it took.

lines.japanese:
己の意志で選んだ道だ。
　後悔はない。
　いや。
lines.english: He had chosen this path of his own will. He had no regrets. No.

lines.japanese:
後悔することを自ら選んだ、とも言える。
　仲間と絆を作るということ。
lines.english: One might equally say he had chosen regret for himself. That was what it meant to forge bonds with companions.

lines.japanese:
それは、つらい思いをせずには通り抜けることの
できない道だ。
lines.english: It was a path no one could travel to its end without enduring pain.

lines.japanese:
だとしてもなお、価値がある。
　維持は獲得よりも難しいものだ。
　世界情勢だって当時とは違う。
lines.english: Even so, it was worth the cost. Keeping something was harder than acquiring it. The state of the world had changed since those days, too.

lines.japanese:
忍は身一つで、やっていかねばならない。
　仲間には内密に、彼らを守ってやらねばならない。
lines.english: Shinobu would have to manage alone. He would have to protect his companions without their knowledge.

lines.japanese: なぜ秘密にするのか？
lines.english: Why keep it secret?

lines.japanese:
章二にしろ葉子にしろ、小さなあずさにしろ、忍
という盾に隠れてよしとしない人種である。
lines.english: Shouji, Youko, even little Azusa—none of them would accept taking shelter behind a shield named Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
彼らを守る。
　それは忍の使命だ。
lines.english: He would protect them. That was Shinobu's mission.

lines.japanese:
守ってもらおうとは思わない。
　残念ながら夜の帝王などと称される章二にしても、
そこまでの力はないはずだ。
lines.english: He had no thought of asking them to protect him. Regrettably, even Shouji, the so-called Emperor of the Night, probably did not have that kind of strength.

lines.japanese:
一番の実力者が守護者であるべきだ。
　だから、忍が守るのだ。
lines.english: The most capable among them should be their guardian. And so Shinobu would protect them.

lines.japanese:
秘められねばならない。
　影ながらでなければならない。
lines.english: It had to remain secret. It had to be done from the shadows.

lines.japanese:
うまくできたからといって、誰に誉められるでも
ない。
lines.english: Even if he did it well, no one would praise him for it.

lines.japanese:
それでも構わないのだった。
　だが、その先は？
lines.english: That was fine with him. But what came after?

lines.japanese: フェンスに背を押しつける。
lines.english: He pressed his back against the fence.

lines.japanese:
もし背もたれが倒れ、真っ逆さまに落下していけ
たら……煩わしさからも解放されるだろうか。
lines.english: If this backrest gave way and sent him plunging headfirst to the ground …would that free him from all this trouble?

lines.japanese: などと、喫水線下の思考を展開してしまう。
lines.english: His thoughts descended below the waterline.

lines.japanese: 人はつらさから自殺する。
lines.english: People killed themselves to escape suffering.

lines.japanese:
圧力を処理できずに、逃げるのだろう。
　だが忍は、
lines.english: Perhaps, unable to handle the pressure, they fled. But Shinobu—

lines.japanese: 「死ねない」
lines.english: “I can't die.”

lines.japanese: 虚空に呟く。
lines.english: He murmured into empty space.

lines.japanese: もとより、死など考えてもいない。
lines.english: He had not actually contemplated death at all.

lines.japanese:
仲間がいる。
　友達がいる。
lines.english: He had companions. He had friends.

lines.japanese:
気がかりをそのままに、自らのスイッチを切るこ
とはできない。
lines.english: He could not switch himself off with his concerns left unattended.

lines.japanese:
手を汚すことになったとしても、ためらいはない
はずだ。
lines.english: Even if it meant dirtying his hands, he would surely not hesitate.

lines.japanese: 「だけど……方法がな」
lines.english: “But… I still need a way.”

lines.japanese:
わからない。
　子供にできることはたかが知れている。
lines.english: He did not know. There was little a child could do.

lines.japanese:
そして大人にだって、そうたいしたことはできな
いものだ。
lines.english: Then again, there was not so very much adults could do either.

lines.japanese: 小さな力を寄り合わせて、なんとか、かんとか。
lines.english: Human beings pooled their meager strength and somehow muddled through.

lines.japanese: 人類史はその一言で説明できてしまいそうだ。
lines.english: Perhaps that one sentence could explain the whole of human history.

lines.japanese:
斎について考える。
　朝はいなかった。
　風邪で休んでいるのだから、当然だ。
lines.english: He thought of Itsuki. Itsuki had not been there that morning. Naturally—he was supposed to be home with a cold.

lines.japanese: それが、いた。
lines.english: And yet, there he was.

lines.japanese:
顔を見ればわかる。
　病弱歴も長い。
　だからわかる。
lines.english: One look at his face was enough. Shinobu had been sickly for a long time himself. He knew.

lines.japanese:
斎は風邪などではない。
　事情があって遅れてきた。
　妹を一人で送り出して。
lines.english: Itsuki did not have a cold. Circumstances had delayed him. He had sent his sister ahead alone.

lines.japanese:
いつも一緒にいたのにである。
　おかしなことではない。
lines.english: They had always been together. Not that this was strange in itself.

lines.japanese:
だからこれは、忍のカンに過ぎない。
　危機が迫っている―――
lines.english: So this was no more than Shinobu's intuition. A crisis was approaching—

lines.japanese:
回避せねばならない。
　せねば、ならない。
lines.english: He had to avert it. He had to.

lines.japanese:
いかな化学物質が促した変化なのか。
　心が、猛烈に不純物を吐き出し始めた。
lines.english: What sort of chemical substance could have prompted the change? His mind began violently purging itself of impurities.

lines.japanese: 「やっと、起動か……」
lines.english: “Finally… It's starting up.”

lines.japanese:
忍は、できるのだった。
　普通に生きていれば、様々なことで汚れ純度を失
っていく心。
lines.english: Shinobu could do it. In the course of an ordinary life, the mind grew sullied by countless things and gradually lost its purity.

lines.japanese:
妖精さえも見通す無垢な貴石も、２０年を過ぎる
頃には傷で濁った石塊。
lines.english: Even a pure jewel capable of seeing fairies would become a clouded, battered lump of stone by the age of twenty.

lines.japanese:
現世を生きるには、それで良い。
　どうせ汚れる人生なのだ。
　繊細さはいらない。
lines.english: That was as it should be in this world. Life would soil you anyway. There was no need to be sensitive.

lines.japanese:
だがもし、純粋さがある種の能力を際だたせる必
要条件であるとすれば。
lines.english: But suppose purity were the necessary condition for bringing a certain faculty into sharp relief.

lines.japanese: 自らの心を純化することが、求められる局面もある。
lines.english: Then there would be moments when one had to purify one's own mind.

lines.japanese:
小さな人の力を、ほんの少しだけ大きなものとす
るために。
lines.english: To make the small power of a human being just a little greater.

lines.japanese:
心は心臓に宿るわけではないが、胸の痛みは意識
の吐く苦痛に思える。
lines.english: The mind did not reside in the heart, yet the pain in his chest felt like his consciousness retching up its distress.

lines.japanese:
まるで絞られるような痛み。
　雫のような汚水が、心の底に落ちていく。
lines.english: A pain as though he were being wrung out. Drops of filthy water fell into the depths of his mind.

lines.japanese: 暗黒の世界。
lines.english: A world of darkness.

lines.japanese:
ありとあらゆる心的なものの墓場に、落ちて霧散
する。
lines.english: They fell into the graveyard of all things born of the mind and dispersed.

lines.japanese:
コバルト色の心を、忍はまざまざと意識した。
　感覚がシャープになっているのがわかる。
lines.english: Shinobu became vividly aware of his cobalt-blue mind. He could feel his senses sharpening.

lines.japanese:
直感の向上。
　思考の強化。
lines.english: Sharpened intuition. Strengthened thought.

lines.japanese:
だがそれだけのものが、今は必要だったのだ。
　自在にとは行かないが、心を研ぎ澄ませることに
特化した人生を歩めるのだ。
lines.english: But for now, that was all he needed. He could not command it at will, but he could devote his life to one thing: honing the mind to a razor’s edge.

lines.japanese: 「……やっとエンジン、かかってきたな……」
lines.english: “…Finally got the engine turning over…”

lines.japanese: うつむいていくつか咳き込み、忍はにんまりと笑う。
lines.english: Shinobu bowed his head, coughed several times, and grinned.

lines.japanese:
敵がいるのなら、戦うための心に切り替える。
　その準備がいよいよ整い始めていた。
　口を大きく開けて、酸素を取り込む。
lines.english: Faced with an enemy, he shifted his mind into a state fit for battle. At long last, the preparations were falling into place. He opened his mouth wide and drew in oxygen.

lines.japanese: 取り込む―――
lines.english: Drew it in—

lines.japanese: 「忍さん」
lines.english: “Shinobu.”
“Hey.”

lines.japanese: 面を持ち上げ、出迎えた。
lines.english: He looked up to greet her.

lines.japanese: 「……お月さまみたい」
lines.english: “…Like the moon.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「青白くて、でも透き通ってて」
lines.english: “Pale blue, but translucent.”

lines.japanese: 「……忍さんの顔」
lines.english: “…Your face.”

lines.japanese: 「ん、苦しそうに見える？」
lines.english: “Do I look like I'm suffering?”

lines.japanese: 「見えます」
lines.english: “You do.”

lines.japanese: 「けど、平気なのかな？　よくわかりません……」
lines.english: “But perhaps you're all right? I cannot tell…”

lines.japanese: 「苦しいのは我慢できるんだよ。慣れるし」
lines.english: “I can bear the pain. And you get used to it.”

lines.japanese: 「慣れない人もいます」
lines.english: “Some people never do.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだね」
lines.english: “True.”

lines.japanese: 「兄、遅れて来てたみたいね」
lines.english: “Your brother came in late, didn't he?”

lines.japanese: 「みたいです」
lines.english: “Apparently.”

lines.japanese: 「よくご存じですね。もう会いました？」
lines.english: “You are well informed. Have you seen him already?”

lines.japanese: 「いや」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 「僕は鈍いけど、カンは良いんだ」
lines.english: “I may be slow, but my intuition is good.”

lines.japanese: 「……ムジュンしています」
lines.english: “…That is a contradiction.”

lines.japanese: 「隠さないで、話しなよ」
lines.english: “Stop hiding it. Tell me.”

lines.japanese:
切り込んだ。
　葉子はしばし黙り込む。
lines.english: He went straight for it. Youko fell silent for a while.

lines.japanese: 「……話すな、と言われていたんですけど……」
lines.english: “…I was told not to tell you…”

lines.japanese: 「斎に？」
lines.english: “By Itsuki?”

lines.japanese: こっくり、と頷く。
lines.english: She gave a small nod.

lines.japanese:
「忍さんが話せというので話しますけど、あとで
　折檻されますから」
lines.english: “I will tell you because you asked me to, but later I will be punished for it.”

lines.japanese: 恩を売るように言う。
lines.english: She said it as though placing him in her debt.

lines.japanese: 「……その分だと、たいしたことなさそうだね」
lines.english: “…From the sound of you, it can't be that serious.”

lines.japanese: 「どうでしょうね？」
lines.english: “Who can say?”

lines.japanese:
「とにかく折檻ですから。そりゃもう。忍さんの言
　うこときいて折檻されるわけですから。ああ、す
　ごくイヤなのに、でも忍さんの頼みですから……」
lines.english: “In any event, I will be punished. Severely. Punished because I obeyed you. Oh, how terribly I dread it, and yet you asked me, Shinobu, so…”

lines.japanese: 「……言うこと何でもきくよ、今度ね」
lines.english: “…Next time, I'll do anything you say.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、何度でも言うこときいてください」
lines.english: “Then you may obey me as many times as I please.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいやいやいや」
lines.english: “No, no, no, no.”

lines.japanese: 「いいから、早く詳細」
lines.english: “Enough of that. Details, now.”

lines.japanese: 「たいしたことじゃありませんです」
lines.english: “It is not anything important, no it is not.”

lines.japanese: 「門倉が戻りました」
lines.english: “Kadokura has returned.”

lines.japanese: 「……うん、そこまでは聞いてる」
lines.english: “…Yes, I've heard that much.”

lines.japanese: 「そのあと、どうなったの？」
lines.english: “What happened after that?”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: こういう時、こともなげに葉子は言う。
lines.english: At times like this, Youko always spoke as though it were nothing.

lines.japanese:
「アレが私の許嫁でしたから、復縁というか、元の
　鞘にサヤッと戻りまして」
lines.english: “He was my betrothed, you see, so now we are back together— the old sword slipped right back into its scabbard, snick.”

lines.japanese:
「あと兄は便利に使える秘書というか側近というか、
　まあカスタムスレイブですよね」
lines.english: “And my brother is a convenient secretary, or perhaps a lieutenant— a custom slave, basically.”

lines.japanese:
「門倉が本格的にいろいろはじめるそうで、学校も
　辞めろということになりまして」
lines.english: “Kadokura apparently intends to start things up in earnest, so the order is to leave school.”

lines.japanese: 「うはは」
lines.english: “Wahaha.”

lines.japanese: 「笑えますよね」
lines.english: “Hilarious, is it not?”

lines.japanese: 「笑えるわけないだろう、ばか」
lines.english: “Of course it isn't funny, you idiot.”

lines.japanese: かたり、葉子の顔が、無機的なものに繰り変わる。
lines.english: With a soft click, Youko's face changed into something inorganic.

lines.japanese:
たとえ喜怒哀楽を形にしなくとも、忍には葉子の
気持ちがよくわかる。
lines.english: Even when no joy, anger, sorrow, or pleasure took shape on her face, Shinobu understood Youko's feelings perfectly.

lines.japanese: 読み取れるのだ。
lines.english: He could read her.

lines.japanese: 「だって、君は泣いてるじゃないか」
lines.english: “Because you're crying.”

lines.japanese: 「飄々としてる風に、見えるけどね」
lines.english: “You may look perfectly unconcerned, though.”

lines.japanese:
「許嫁・秘書・退学。簡単に君は言うけど……
　看過できることじゃないでしょ」
lines.english: “Betrothal. Secretary. Dropping out. You say it so casually… but none of it can be overlooked.”

lines.japanese: 「絶対に見逃せないことだ。ふざけるなだ」
lines.english: “We absolutely can't let any of that pass. That's a definite ‘screw that.’”
“But…”

lines.japanese: 「たいへんな時だよ。こんな時代だよ」
lines.english: “These are hard times. That's the kind of age we're living in.”

lines.japanese: 「僕だって、こんなザマだしね」
lines.english: “I'm in this sorry state myself.”

lines.japanese: 「けど、ねぇ？」
lines.english: “But still. Right?”

lines.japanese: 「……関わったら、怪我しますから……」
lines.english: “…If you become involved, you will be hurt…”

lines.japanese: 「するかもしれないね」
lines.english: “Perhaps I will.”

lines.japanese: 「社会的にマッサツされるかも」
lines.english: “You may be socially ANNIHILATED.”

lines.japanese: 「されるかもしれないねぇ」
lines.english: “Perhaps I will.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、」
lines.english: “So—”

lines.japanese:
面を伏せて、もう何も言わない。
　頑迷な忍を説得できないと、充分に葉子は知って
いる。
lines.english: She lowered her face and said no more. Youko knew perfectly well that Shinobu, stubborn as he was, could not be persuaded.

lines.japanese: 「僕が危険だから、隠そうとしていた……か」
lines.english: “So you tried to hide it because getting involved would put me in danger…”

lines.japanese: 「門倉が帰ってきたことは斎に聞いたんだ」
lines.english: “Itsuki told me Kadokura was back.”

lines.japanese:
「そうやって、情報を小出しにして、もっと大切な
　ことを隠そうとした」
lines.english: “You fed me that information bit by bit to hide something even more important.”

lines.japanese: 「……僕が関わらないように」
lines.english: “…To keep me from getting involved.”

lines.japanese:
「確かに……頼りないかも知れないけど、何もでき
　ないとは思わないな」
lines.english: “I may not be very dependable… but I don’t believe I’m entirely helpless.”

lines.japanese: 「私たちは、我慢する必要も……ないんです」
lines.english: “We do not even need… to endure it.”

lines.japanese: とつとつと口にする。
lines.english: She spoke haltingly.

lines.japanese: 「元通りになるだけですからね」
lines.english: “Things will merely return to the way they were.”

lines.japanese: 「その元を、壊したのは僕だ」
lines.english: “I'm the one who put an end to the way things were.”

lines.japanese: 「……知ってました」
lines.english: “…I knew.”

lines.japanese: 「斎に聞いた？　それとも自分で調べた？」
lines.english: “Did Itsuki tell you? Or did you investigate?”

lines.japanese:
「どっちも違います。
　けど……なんとなくわかりました」
lines.english: “Neither. But… somehow, I understood.”

lines.japanese:
「僕は、珍しい病気だからね。その関係で、保健と
　か医療関係にいろいろとコネがあるんだよ」
lines.english: “I have a rare illness. Because of it, I've made all sorts of connections in health care and medicine.”

lines.japanese:
「注射嫌いの僕が、献血一回と引き替えに、どれだ
　けの“お願い”ができるか……
　君は知らないだろう？」
lines.english: “I hate needles, but you have no idea how many favors I can ask for in exchange for a single blood donation… do you?”

lines.japanese:
葉子は迷った。
　忍の言葉をどれだけ信じていいものか、迷った。
lines.english: Youko hesitated. She wondered how much of Shinobu's claim she could believe.

lines.japanese:
もし、言うとおりに大きな力を行使できるのであ
れば……と。
lines.english: What if he truly could wield power on the scale he claimed…?

lines.japanese: 絶望が無気力にする。
lines.english: Despair sapped a person of all will.

lines.japanese:
そして一片の希望が、深い闇の淵で人を稼働させ
もする。
lines.english: Yet a single shard of hope could set that person in motion at the edge of the deepest darkness.

lines.japanese: 葉子に本音を、吐瀉させもする。
lines.english: It could even make Youko vomit up what she truly felt.

lines.japanese: 「忍さん……」
lines.english: “Shinobu…”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「本、当に？」
lines.english: “Is that—really true?”

lines.japanese: 「正直ね」
lines.english: “I mean it.”

lines.japanese: 立ち上がる。
lines.english: He stood.

lines.japanese:
頭痛はもう、気にならなくなっていた。
　階段を上り下りするたびに、ズキズキと痛む。そ
れは変わりない。
lines.english: The headache no longer occupied his attention. It still throbbed whenever he climbed or descended the stairs. That had not changed.

lines.japanese:
だが受け皿である精神が強まれば、どうというこ
ともない。
lines.english: But once the mind that bore it grew stronger, the pain was nothing.

lines.japanese:
彼を駆り立てるものは何かだ。
　忍を先鋭にしたものは怒りだ。
lines.english: What was it that drove him? What had honed Shinobu to this edge was anger.

lines.japanese: 忍は七人という個体の、いわば免疫機構になる。
lines.english: Shinobu would become, as it were, the immune system of the single organism composed of all seven.

lines.japanese:
外敵を排する機能。
　外との戦い。
lines.english: A mechanism for expelling foreign threats. The war against the outside.

lines.japanese: （それが……病的な構図であったとしても）
lines.english: (Even if… the arrangement itself is pathological.)

lines.japanese:
かつて忍は、侵略行為を肯定していた。
　むしろ、無駄な努力はするべきではないという
スタンス。
lines.english: Once, Shinobu had condoned acts of invasion. More than that, his position had been that one should not waste effort on futile resistance.

lines.japanese: 外敵が強大であるなら、結果などは見えている。
lines.english: If the outside enemy was overwhelmingly powerful, the result was plain.

lines.japanese:
結果が見えている。
　ならば、あとはどう過ごすか、だけではないか。
lines.english: The result was already known. Then the only question remaining was how to spend the time before it came.

lines.japanese:
明日核戦争で全てが終わります。あなたはどう過
ごしますか？
lines.english: Tomorrow, nuclear war will end everything. How will you spend your final day?

lines.japanese:
そんな仮想に似ている。
　人間らしく。
lines.english: It was that sort of thought experiment. Spend it as a human being.

lines.japanese:
忍が選択するだろう答えは、それだ。
　現実に当てはめてみる。
lines.english: That was the answer Shinobu would choose. Now he applied it to reality.

lines.japanese: 仲間を優先する。何よりも―――
lines.english: He would place his companions before all else—

lines.japanese:
そういうことになる。
　忍は、免疫抗体としては適した人材とは言えない。
lines.english: That was what it came down to. Shinobu could hardly be called an ideal antibody.

lines.japanese:
そういう自覚はある。
　樋口章二のような男にこそ、ふさわしい役目には
違いない。
lines.english: He was aware of that. The role undoubtedly suited a man like Shouji Higuchi far better.

lines.japanese:
冷静に戦える人間だからだ。
　だが今、忍の心は烈火に焦げついている。
lines.english: Shouji was capable of fighting with a cool head. But now Shinobu's mind was scorched by a raging fire.

lines.japanese:
彼を励起させた、二つのキーワード。
　許嫁。そして奴隷。
lines.english: Two words had triggered this state in him. Betrothed. And slave.

lines.japanese:
いずれも略奪を意味する言葉、見過ごすことので
きない概念。
lines.english: Both were words for plunder— concepts he could not overlook.

lines.japanese: 「……忍さん」
lines.english: “…Shinobu.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「門倉は……忍さんのこと、知ってるみたいです」
lines.english: “Kadokura… seems to know about you.”

lines.japanese: 「面識はほとんどないんだけどね」
lines.english: “We've barely even met.”

lines.japanese:
「調べたみたいです。あの当時、起こったことにつ
　いて」
lines.english: “It seems he investigated what happened at that time.”

lines.japanese: 「……まったく、千鳥姉さんもツメが甘いよ」
lines.english: “…Honestly, Chidori left too many loose ends.”

lines.japanese:
「だから、教師にイジメの相談しようなんて人間が、
　いなくなるんだ」
lines.english: “No wonder nobody wants to go to a teacher about being bullied.”

lines.japanese:
金網に指先を走らせる忍を、葉子は決意を込めた
瞳で見た。
lines.english: Youko watched Shinobu run his fingertips along the fence, resolution in her eyes.

lines.japanese: 「……兄もだいぶ参っているみたいなんです」
lines.english: “…My brother seems to be taking it rather badly too.”
“…Itsuki?”

lines.japanese:
「はい。表には出さないんですが……特に私の婚約
　について、胸を痛めているみたいで」
lines.english: “Yes. He does not show it… but my engagement in particular seems to be causing him pain.”

lines.japanese: 「不器用な人間ですからね、あれは」
lines.english: “He is terribly clumsy with things like that.”

lines.japanese: 「だよね」
lines.english: “He is.”

lines.japanese: 「……呆れるくらい、不器用だよねぇ」
lines.english: “…Clumsy enough to make you shake your head.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 二人は顔を見合わせて、小さく笑った。
lines.english: They exchanged a look and shared a small laugh.

lines.japanese: 「自分を追いつめないといいけど……」
lines.english: “I hope he doesn't drive himself into a corner…”

lines.japanese:
「だから兄の力は期待できない。厳しいことになり
　そうですよ？」
lines.english: “Which means we cannot rely upon my brother's help. This is likely to be difficult, you know?”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫」
lines.english: “It'll be fine.”

lines.japanese:
根拠のない言葉だった。
　葉子の台詞の方が、はるかに現実的であった。
lines.english: He had no grounds for saying so. Youko was being far more realistic.

lines.japanese: （でもやらなきゃ）
lines.english: (But I have to do it.)

lines.japanese:
（抱えきれない悩み、問題……
　ひとつひとつ、解決していかないと）
lines.english: (More troubles and problems than I can carry… I have to resolve them one at a time.)
(Steadily—)

lines.japanese: （僕には何の力もない）
lines.english: (I have no power at all.)

lines.japanese:
（……持っているものをうまく使って、確実にやっ
　ていかないといけない）
lines.english: (…I have to make the best use of what I do have and move forward one sure step at a time.)

lines.japanese:
もっとも明晰な自分を引き出し、着実に、コマを
進めていく。
lines.english: He would summon the most lucid version of himself and advance his pieces, one sure move at a time.

lines.japanese:
冴えてはいないが、たった一つのやり方には違い
ない。
lines.english: It was hardly ingenious, but it was the only method available to him.

lines.japanese: 「信じてくれる？」
lines.english: “Will you trust me?”

lines.japanese: 「……本当に、もう」
lines.english: “Honestly, you…”

lines.japanese: 口元を押さえて、ぷっ、と葉子は笑った。
lines.english: Covering her mouth, Youko gave a little burst of laughter.

lines.japanese: 「すごく、気持ちがいいですよ、今」
lines.english: “I feel remarkably good right now.”
“…Oh. You do?”

lines.japanese:
「どんな結果になっても、私は後悔しないですみそ
　うです」
lines.english: “Whatever happens, I believe I shall have no regrets.”
“Youko…”

lines.japanese:
あまりにも晴れやかに言われ、絶句した。
　彼女は奇跡など期待していない。
lines.english: She said it with such radiance that he was struck speechless. She expected no miracle.

lines.japanese:
起こるべきが起こる、おさまるところにおさまる。
　そして忍の決意が、それはそれとして、嬉しい。
lines.english: What must happen would happen; everything would settle where it must. Whatever else might happen, Shinobu's resolve itself made her happy.

lines.japanese: だから満足だと、言っているようなものであった。
lines.english: It was as though she were saying that alone was enough for her.

lines.japanese: 「結果は出すよ」
lines.english: “I'll get results.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「出すんだってば」
lines.english: “I said I will.”

lines.japanese: 「ですから、はい」
lines.english: “Like I said, yes.”

lines.japanese: 「……まいったな」
lines.english: “…You've got me.”

lines.japanese: 悟られてしまった。
lines.english: She had seen straight through him.

lines.japanese:
なんだか、助けようと必死になっている自分の方
が、青いような。
lines.english: Somehow, he—the one so desperate to save her— seemed the more naive of the two.

lines.japanese: 「結果より過程重視派」
lines.english: “I vote for process over results.”

lines.japanese: と手をあげるものだから、
lines.english: She raised her hand to cast her vote, so—

lines.japanese: 「過程と結果のどっちも重視派」
lines.english: “I vote for both process and results.”

lines.japanese: 「よくばり」
lines.english: “Selfish.”

lines.japanese: 指をさされる。
lines.english: She pointed at him.

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ？」
lines.english: “So what if I am?”

lines.japanese: ちょっぴりムキになる。
lines.english: He was getting a little defensive.

lines.japanese: 「まえばり」
lines.english: “Shelf bra.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめん……わかんない」
lines.english: “Sorry… I don't follow.”

lines.japanese: 拙く話す二人を、空は祝福も呪いもしない。
lines.english: The sky neither blessed nor cursed the two as they stumbled through their conversation.

lines.japanese: （こんな日常）
lines.english: (This ordinary life.)

lines.japanese: そして忍は、
lines.english: And so Shinobu—

lines.japanese: （壊させない―――）
lines.english: (I won't let anyone destroy it.)

lines.japanese:
決意を、秘めた。
　声を、出した。
lines.english: He kept that resolve to himself. Then he spoke.

lines.japanese: 「待機命令」
lines.english: “Stand by for orders.”

lines.japanese: 「……ふわぁ」
lines.english: “…Yaaawn.”

lines.japanese: 二人は、天と地の間に横たわって、昼寝をしていた。
lines.english: The two lay between earth and sky, napping in the afternoon.

lines.japanese:
忍に誘われたのだから、自発というのは違うかも
知れないが……似たようなものだ。
lines.english: Shinobu had invited him, so perhaps Itsuki had not come entirely of his own accord… Still, it came to much the same thing.

lines.japanese:
決めたのは、自分なのだから。
　二人はうつらうつらとしながら、流れる雲を眺め
ている。
lines.english: The choice was his, after all. Half asleep, the two of them watched the clouds drift by.

lines.japanese: いざという時に何を捨てるのか。
lines.english: What would you cast aside when the time came?

lines.japanese:
忍が先ほど言った言葉を、斎は反芻している。
　思考は堂々巡り。
　結論は出ない。
lines.english: Itsuki kept turning Shinobu's earlier words over in his mind. His thoughts ran in circles. He could reach no answer.

lines.japanese:
体を動かせるほどには、脳が働かない。
　むくと身を起こす。
lines.english: His brain was not working well enough to get him moving. He sat up.

lines.japanese: しかし何を語るでもなく、ぼんやりと前を見ている。
lines.english: But Itsuki said nothing, only gazed blankly ahead.

lines.japanese: 言葉などない。
lines.english: No words.

lines.japanese: が、忍は察した。
lines.english: Shinobu understood all the same.

lines.japanese: 斎の胸中に渦巻く、もやもやした何かを。
lines.english: He sensed the vague, restless feeling churning inside Itsuki.

lines.japanese: 「斎は……剣道やってたよね」
lines.english: “You used to practice kendo, didn't you, Itsuki?”

lines.japanese:
正確には剣道ではないが、わざわざ訂正するほど
のことでもない。
lines.english: Strictly speaking, it was not kendo, but that hardly seemed worth correcting.

lines.japanese: 斎は首を振った。
lines.english: Itsuki shook his head.

lines.japanese: 「よし」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 忍は立ち上がった。
lines.english: Shinobu stood up.

lines.japanese: 「なら、さらに強くなるための必殺技を伝授するよ」
lines.english: “Then I'll teach you a secret move that'll make you even stronger.”

lines.japanese:
重い沈黙があった。
　確かに斎は、古武道の修練を積んでいる。
lines.english: A heavy silence followed. Itsuki had, indeed, trained in an old school of martial arts.

lines.japanese:
戦国時代の白兵戦で研鑽された武器術のみばかり
か、素手による組み討ちはもちろん、建物内部への
突入に関する一連の段取り、
lines.english: The school went far beyond weapons techniques honed in the close combat of the Warring States period: it taught unarmed grappling, of course, as well as the full procedure for storming a building,

lines.japanese: 逆に襲撃された場合の対処術などにも及ぶ。
lines.english: and, conversely, how to respond when attacked.

lines.japanese:
また近代以降、戦時に培われた軍刀操作術も取り
込みつつ、不合理な部分を排除したものだ。
lines.english: It had also incorporated military saber techniques developed in modern warfare, stripping away anything impractical.

lines.japanese:
だが実践一本かといえば、そうでもなかった。
　不意打ちなどの暗殺術に属する部分等、
lines.english: Yet practical combat was not its only concern. Techniques of assassination, such as surprise attacks,

lines.japanese:
他流派で禁じ手とされるようなものは同流派の
“凶”に分類され、それを身につけるのは身分の低
い者の分担となった。
lines.english: forbidden in other schools, were classed here as “Sinister.” Learning them was the duty of those of lower standing.

lines.japanese: 即ち斎がそうである。
lines.english: Itsuki was one of them.

lines.japanese:
斎が習う技は、抜き付けと呼ばれる脛への攻撃、
手先に対する指落とし、逃亡者の腱を断つ追い斬り、
lines.english: Itsuki chiefly trained in the draw cut, a strike to the shin; finger severing, aimed at the hand; and the pursuit cut, used to slice a fugitive's tendons;

lines.japanese:
暗闇における刀剣操法（暗殺術）などが主立った
ものである。
lines.english: and swordsmanship in darkness—in other words, assassination. Those were the principal techniques.

lines.japanese:
逆に表の技は、儀仗としての側面が強い。
　華々しさを求めるあまり、ときに実戦からも外れ
てしまっている技も多い。
lines.english: The public branch, by contrast, was largely ceremonial. In pursuit of splendor, many of its techniques had strayed from the realities of combat.

lines.japanese:
門倉に由緒があることには疑う余地もなく、これ
らが王者のための技であることは納得がいく。
lines.english: The Kadokura lineage was ancient beyond question, and it made sense that these arts had been designed for rulers.

lines.japanese:
上に立つ者は露払いをしない。
　雑兵に囲まれることもなければ、馬上から降りる
ことも少ない。
lines.english: Those at the top do not clear the way themselves. They are never surrounded by common soldiers, and seldom come down from horseback.

lines.japanese:
そうでなければならなかった。
　逆に、一対一の正面からの戦闘では、必勝が要求
された。
lines.english: That was how it had to be. But in single combat, face-to-face, nothing short of victory would do.

lines.japanese:
全ての戦場に武士道があったわけではない。
　が、戦国時代を過ぎて熟成された礼節の概念は、
門倉の思想にはまことによく馴染んだ。
lines.english: Bushido did not rule every battlefield. Yet the code of courtesy that matured after the Warring States period meshed perfectly with the Kadokura school's philosophy.

lines.japanese:
そして表裏の区分によって、両系統が剥離を起こ
しているとさえ思えるほどの、激烈な分岐を招いた。
lines.english: Dividing the tradition into public and hidden forms sent the two branches down such violently different paths that they seemed all but severed from each other.

lines.japanese:
表の技は決闘に特化したものとなり、しかも扱い
に熟練を要す。
lines.english: The public arts specialized in dueling and demanded great skill of the practitioner.

lines.japanese:
凶の技は闇討ちや雑兵相手のものであり、華を去
りて実に就く、習得も比較的容易なものである。
lines.english: The Sinister arts, meant for ambushes and fighting common soldiers, discarded beauty for utility. They were also relatively easy to learn.

lines.japanese: ……そこに、華麗な技などはないのである。
lines.english: …There was no splendor in them.

lines.japanese: あるのはただ、実直な、殺害の術。
lines.english: Only the plain, straightforward art of killing.

lines.japanese:
完全な形で凶を修めた者は、呼吸をするように殺
傷を操作できるだろう。
lines.english: Someone who had mastered the Sinister arts could inflict injury or death as naturally as breathing.

lines.japanese:
そんなようなことを、差し障りのない範囲で、斎
は説明した。
lines.english: Itsuki explained all this— or as much of it as he was at liberty to share.

lines.japanese: 「……そう、確かにそれは、確実な武道だね」
lines.english: “…I see. It certainly sounds effective.”

lines.japanese:
「でも斎はまだそれを完全に身につけてはいないん
　じゃない？」
lines.english: “But you haven't mastered it completely yet, have you?”

lines.japanese: 確かに技術的な面で、いくつかの問題を抱えている。
lines.english: True, a few technical problems remained.

lines.japanese:
忍の言うとおりである。
　しかしだからといって斎が思い悩むほどの問題で
はなかった。
lines.english: Shinobu was right. But they were hardly serious enough to weigh on Itsuki.

lines.japanese:
幼い者が未熟なのは当然だ。
　持続するうちに身につければ良いのである。
lines.english: It was only natural for a child to be unskilled. He would master it if he kept at it.

lines.japanese:
少なくとも元服とされる年齢までは、誰も斎に一
人前を求めることはない。
lines.english: At least until he came of age, no one expected Itsuki to be a full-fledged practitioner.

lines.japanese:
だから忍の発言には、疑問がつきまとう。
　そもそも武道の経験が、忍にはあるのかどうか？
lines.english: That was why Shinobu's comment nagged at him. Had Shinobu ever practiced martial arts himself?

lines.japanese: 「斎には、才能があると思う」
lines.english: “I think you've got talent, Itsuki.”

lines.japanese:
「え？　刀もなしに剣道の必殺技もないだろう
　って？　いらないんだよ、この技は。刀なんて」
lines.english: “Huh? You mean it can't be a secret kendo move if there's no sword? This move doesn't need one. Who needs a sword?”

lines.japanese: と、忍は腰を落とし、手刀を立てて構える。
lines.english: Shinobu sank into a stance with one knife-hand held upright.

lines.japanese: 「だって刀なんて、持ち歩けないじゃないか」
lines.english: “It's not like you can walk around carrying a sword.”

lines.japanese: 黙り込む。
lines.english: Itsuki fell silent.

lines.japanese:
もちろん組み討ちだって斎の領分だ。
　そして知る限りにおいて、手刀ひとつによる必殺
技など、まともな流派にはありはしない。
lines.english: Itsuki's training included grappling, of course. And as far as he knew, no respectable school had any such thing as a secret finishing move delivered with a single knife-hand.

lines.japanese:
「この技は……そうだね、
　僕はこういうのは詳しくないけど……
　クビキリブレードとでも名付けようか」
lines.english: “This move… let's see… I don't know much about this kind of thing, but… how about the Neck-Cutter Blade?”

lines.japanese: 斎は吹いた。
lines.english: Itsuki snorted.

lines.japanese: 「なぜ笑う……？」
lines.english: “Why are you laughing…?”

lines.japanese:
「え？　伝授する側なら技の名前くらい知って
　おけ？　いや、これは今つけたから……」
lines.english: “Huh? If I'm teaching you, I should at least know its name? I just made that name up…”

lines.japanese: 斎は腹を抱えて丸くなり、肩を震わせた。
lines.english: Itsuki hunched over clutching his stomach, shoulders shaking.

lines.japanese: 「……教えないよ」
lines.english: “…I'm not teaching you.”

lines.japanese:
詫びを入れ、斎は立ち上がった。
　晴れやかな笑顔。
lines.english: Itsuki apologized and stood up. His smile was radiant.

lines.japanese:
必殺技はさぞかし稚拙なものだろう。
　いや、だからこそ……斎はそれを伝授してもらい
たくなった。
lines.english: It was bound to be a laughably childish move. No—that was exactly why Itsuki wanted to learn it from Shinobu.

lines.japanese: 「……ＯＫ。やっと教えられるよ」
lines.english: “…Okay. Now I can finally teach you.”

lines.japanese:
「えーと、細かいことはわからないんだけど……こ
　れは、けっこうできる人も多いんだ。本当だよ」
lines.english: “Um, I don't know all the details, but… actually, quite a few people can do this. I'm serious.”

lines.japanese: 「人間の首はね、極めれば素手で落とせるんだって」
lines.english: “They say that once you master it, you can take a person's head off with your bare hands.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　違う、ゲームのニンジャの話ではなく」
lines.english: “Huh? No, I don't mean those ninjas from video games.”

lines.japanese: 「……信じられてない……のか……？」
lines.english: “…You… don't believe me…?”

lines.japanese: 「どうやるのかって？　やり方は簡単なんだ」
lines.english: “You want to know how? It's simple.”

lines.japanese: 忍はとんでもないことを口走った。
lines.english: Then Shinobu said something preposterous.

lines.japanese: 「気合いをこめて手刀で首筋を叩くんだ」
lines.english: “You focus all your energy and strike the side of the neck with a knife-hand.”

lines.japanese: 爆笑された。
lines.english: Itsuki exploded with laughter.

lines.japanese:
「…………あぁ、そうか、この感情が、
　イライラってやつか……なるほど」
lines.english: “…Oh. So this feeling… is what people call irritation… I see.”

lines.japanese:
憮然とした忍をよそに、斎は腹の底から笑い声を
あげた。
lines.english: Ignoring Shinobu's sour look, Itsuki let out a deep belly laugh.

lines.japanese:
笑う斎。
　不機嫌な自分。
lines.english: Itsuki, laughing. Himself, sulking.

lines.japanese:
そんな構図を自覚してか、次第に忍のうちに温か
なものが湧き起こった。
lines.english: Perhaps that contrast was what made something warm gradually rise within Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
存在は知っていても使ったことのない言葉がいく
つかあって、うち一つを口にしてみようと、たわむ
れに思わせた。
lines.english: There were a few words Shinobu knew but had never used. On a playful whim, he decided to try one now.

lines.japanese: 「斎ムカつく」
lines.english: “You piss me off, Itsuki.”

lines.japanese:
斎はさらに声をあげた。
　普段のイメージと、違いすぎたせいだろう。
lines.english: That only made Itsuki laugh louder. Perhaps it was simply so unlike the Shinobu he knew.

lines.japanese: （お互い……あんなに、そっけなかったのに……な）
lines.english: (We were both… so distant from each other… and yet.)

lines.japanese:
しばらくの間、忍は斎の朗笑を見守る。
　不思議と満たされた顔で。
lines.english: For a while, Shinobu watched Itsuki laugh freely, a strangely contented look on his face.

lines.japanese:
やがて頃合いを見計らって、怒りからではない皮
肉を投げかけた。
lines.english: Then he chose his moment and tossed Itsuki a barb— one with no anger behind it.

lines.japanese:
「君の修行というのは、笑うことなの？
　そろそろはじめない？」
lines.english: “Is laughing part of your training? Don't you think we should get started?”

lines.japanese: 笑い声がようやく押さえ込まれて―――向き直る。
lines.english: At last Itsuki got his laughter under control—and turned to face him.

lines.japanese: 「悪い悪い。怒るな」
lines.english: “Sorry, sorry. Don't be mad.”

lines.japanese: 「……怒ってなんかいないよ」
lines.english: “…I'm not mad.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか？」
lines.english: “You're not?”

lines.japanese:
「それでどうするのかな、僕は伝授した方がいい？
　それともやめた方がいい？」
lines.english: “So what's it going to be? Do you want me to teach you, or should we forget it?”

lines.japanese: 「教えてくれ」
lines.english: “Teach me.”

lines.japanese: 「やっと本題に入れたね」
lines.english: “Now we can finally get to it.”

lines.japanese: 「素手で首を落とすんだって？」
lines.english: “You can really take someone's head off with your bare hands?”

lines.japanese: 「完全に落とすには、たくさん才能がいるけどね」
lines.english: “Getting it all the way off takes an awful lot of talent, though.”

lines.japanese:
「まあ……あるかも知れないと思えないこともない
　けどな」
lines.english: “Well… I can't say it couldn't exist.”

lines.japanese:
「昔の人間は戦いの中に生きていたわけだし、ある
　いは」
lines.english: “People in the old days lived in the midst of war, so maybe…”

lines.japanese: 「斎はどうかな。それくらいあれば、できるかも」
lines.english: “I wonder about you, Itsuki. With that much, you just might manage it.”

lines.japanese: 「それとは？」
lines.english: “That much what?”

lines.japanese: 「……うーん、才能、というか、素質、というか」
lines.english: “…Hmm. Talent, maybe. Or natural aptitude.”

lines.japanese: 「あると言われて嬉しいものの一つだな」
lines.english: “That’s one of those things it’s nice to be told you have.”

lines.japanese: 「ただ俺、稽古ではいまいちだって言われてるぞ？」
lines.english: “But I'm told I don't do so well in training.”

lines.japanese:
「いいんだ、そっちの素質はいらない。
　まず、首を叩く角度だけど……」
lines.english: “That's all right. You don't need that sort of aptitude. First, the angle when you strike the neck…”

lines.japanese:
そして話しはじめた内容は。
　荒唐無稽なようでいて、どこか楽しげで、それは
まるで、
lines.english: And then Shinobu began. What followed sounded preposterous, yet somehow playful— almost like

lines.japanese: 御伽噺のような―――
lines.english: a fairy tale—

lines.japanese: 門倉正道という人物は、当時忍より四つ上だった。
lines.english: Seidou Kadokura was four years older than Shinobu at the time.

lines.japanese:
当然、学校も異なってくる。
　しかし地域を同じくする学校群は連なることがある。
lines.english: Naturally, they attended different schools. But schools in the same district sometimes formed networks of their own.

lines.japanese: 門倉もその口だ。
lines.english: Kadokura belonged to one such network.

lines.japanese:
地元の富豪。嫡子。
　地域一帯の不良グループを束ねていた。
lines.english: A local tycoon's son and heir. He held sway over the delinquent groups throughout the district.

lines.japanese:
子供らしからぬ金と人脈を用いたグループは、犯
罪性の薄い、義賊的な集団と化した。
lines.english: Using money and connections far beyond what one would expect of children, the group became a band of Robin Hoods with very little actual crime to its name.

lines.japanese:
それはステータスだった。
　子供世界における絶対的な価値観。
　属するべき、目指すべき有り様。
lines.english: Membership conferred status. In the world of children, it was an absolute measure of worth: the thing to join, the thing to aspire to.

lines.japanese:
家族より、学校より。
　組織には当然、属する見返りがあるものだ。
lines.english: Above family. Above school. And naturally, an organization gave its members something in return.

lines.japanese:
圧倒的な庇護という形で。
　反面、公然と刃向かう者が制裁を受けることは多
かった。
lines.english: Overwhelming protection. On the other hand, those who openly defied it were often punished.

lines.japanese:
土地柄も、それを容認したのである。
　実際彼らは敵対する集団には、容赦がなかった。
lines.english: The local culture allowed it. And indeed, they showed rival groups no mercy.

lines.japanese:
そして活動は、表だった少年犯罪を取り締まる結
果になった。
lines.english: In practice, their activities kept the more conspicuous forms of juvenile crime in check.

lines.japanese: 子供の倫理によって、秩序がもたらされたのだ。
lines.english: The children's own code had brought order.

lines.japanese: 彼らの存在を、一般の大人達が知ることはなかった。
lines.english: Ordinary adults never even knew they existed.

lines.japanese:
巧妙な子供の倫理によって隠蔽された。
　同じ土地に異なる世界が重なっているように。
lines.english: The children's own subtle code kept them hidden. It was as though two different worlds occupied the same ground.

lines.japanese:
大人たちの現実と、子供らの幻想。
　両者の境は常に揺らぎ、安定しない。
lines.english: Adult reality and childhood fantasy. The boundary between them never settled, forever wavering.

lines.japanese:
少年たちは、時間をかけて少しずつ夢から覚めて
いくものだ。
lines.english: Given time, boys awaken from that dream little by little.

lines.japanese:
例外はない。
　あるとすれば、もはや人としての適切さを放棄し
なければならない。
lines.english: There are no exceptions. Any exception would have to give up all claim to being a proper human being.

lines.japanese:
しかし門倉の帝国が、長く繁栄したこともまた事
実である。
lines.english: And yet Kadokura's empire flourished for many years.

lines.japanese: 昼休み、三人の空気はどこまでも停滞している。
lines.english: At lunch, the air among the three of them had gone utterly still.

lines.japanese:
三角形を描いてにらみ合っている。
　周囲に人影はない。
lines.english: The three stood in a triangle, glaring at one another. No one else was around.

lines.japanese:
校庭でも寂れた場所だ。
　兎小屋が近く、多少臭う。
lines.english: It was a deserted corner of the schoolyard. The rabbit hutch stood nearby, lending the air a faint stink.

lines.japanese:
見つめ合っている。
　三すくみだ。
lines.english: They kept staring. A three-way standoff.

lines.japanese:
緊張が見られた。
　しかしどこか滑稽な様相をも帯びている。
lines.english: There was unmistakable tension. Yet the scene had something faintly ridiculous about it.

lines.japanese: 「はじめてだな」
lines.english: “This is a first.”

lines.japanese:
やがて、斎がため息まじりに言う。
　根負けした、という印象。
lines.english: Eventually Itsuki spoke, sighing. He sounded as though he had finally yielded.

lines.japanese: 「……遊びの押し売りというのは」
lines.english: “…Having someone force me to play.”

lines.japanese: 「こっちもだよ」
lines.english: “It's a first for me too.”

lines.japanese:
葉子はぼんやりしていた。
　視線が彷徨っている。
　瞳に浮かぶゴミを追っている可能性があった。
lines.english: Youko stared into space. Her gaze drifted aimlessly. Perhaps she was following a floater across her vision.

lines.japanese: 「目的は？」
lines.english: “What are you after?”

lines.japanese: 「友達が、欲しい」
lines.english: “I want friends.”

lines.japanese: 「……貴宮、だったな」
lines.english: “…Atemiya, right?”

lines.japanese: 「貴宮忍」
lines.english: “Shinobu Atemiya.”

lines.japanese:
「おまえが俺たちに近づいた理由を、俺は想像して
　みたよ」
lines.english: “I've been trying to work out why you came up to us.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえは……党に入りたいんじゃないのか？」
lines.english: “You… want to join the Party, don't you?”
“The Party?”

lines.japanese: 「知らないはずはない」
lines.english: “There's no way you don't know.”

lines.japanese: 「この町に住むなら」
lines.english: “Not if you live in this town.”

lines.japanese: 「知らない」
lines.english: “I don't know.”

lines.japanese:
「……見え透いている。
　もっとましな嘘でなければ―――」
lines.english: “…I can see right through you. If you're going to lie, at least make it convincing—”

lines.japanese: 「本当に知らないよ。引っ越してきたばかりだから」
lines.english: “I really don't. I only just moved here.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
「知ってる知らないの言い争いはいいや。
　で、党ってのは何？」
lines.english: “Never mind arguing about whether I know. What's the Party?”

lines.japanese: 「……知らないのか」
lines.english: “…You really don't know.”

lines.japanese: 「知らない。党？　なんの党だって？」
lines.english: “I don't. The Party? What kind of party are you talking about?”

lines.japanese:
斎はしばし渋面で忍を見つめていた。
　が、観念したように口を開いた。
lines.english: Itsuki studied Shinobu for a while, scowling. Then, with an air of resignation, he began to explain.

lines.japanese: 「ただの党だ。名前なんかはない」
lines.english: “It's just the Party. It doesn't have a name.”

lines.japanese:
「言ってみれば少年チームだな。ただ野球やサッカー
　をするためのものじゃない」
lines.english: “You could call it a youth group. Except it isn't just for playing baseball or soccer.”

lines.japanese: 「……じゃあ、何を？」
lines.english: “…Then what is it for?”

lines.japanese: 「遊びだ」
lines.english: “For fun.”

lines.japanese: 拍子抜けする思いだった。
lines.english: The answer was an anticlimax.

lines.japanese: 「遊びって、どんな？」
lines.english: “What kind of fun?”

lines.japanese:
「子供同士のいろんな問題を仕切ったり、
　暴れすぎた連中をシめたり、ごくたまには多少の
　無茶もする」
lines.english: “We handle all kinds of problems between kids, put people in their place when they get too wild, and every now and then we do something a little crazy.”

lines.japanese:
「だからケンカの強いやつや、頭の良いヤツは取り
　込まれる」
lines.english: “That's why anyone who's good in a fight or especially smart gets recruited.”

lines.japanese: 「不良グループ？」
lines.english: “A delinquent gang?”

lines.japanese:
「近いが、違うな。もっとまとまってる。そして表
　だって悪さはしない」
lines.english: “Close, but not quite. We're more organized. And we don't make trouble out in the open.”

lines.japanese: 「トップの人間が、うるさいからな」
lines.english: “The guy at the top is strict about that.”

lines.japanese: 「いいものに聞こえる……」
lines.english: “It sounds like a good thing…”

lines.japanese: 「仁義、と言ってわかるか」
lines.english: “Do you know what honor and duty mean?”

lines.japanese: 「仁義ね」
lines.english: “Honor and duty.”

lines.japanese: 「仁義ごっこ、といったところか。今のところは」
lines.english: “You could say we're playing at honor and duty. For now.”

lines.japanese: 「……そのうち、違うものになるってこと？」
lines.english: “…You mean it'll turn into something else eventually?”

lines.japanese: 「リーダーにとってはな」
lines.english: “For the leader, it will.”

lines.japanese: 「将来に、その人間関係を使うんだよ。わかるか？」
lines.english: “He'll use all those connections later. Understand?”

lines.japanese: 「わかる」
lines.english: “I understand.”

lines.japanese:
「……そういうのは、大人の世界で役に立つんだっ
　てことだ」
lines.english: “…They'll be useful in the adult world someday. That's what you mean.”

lines.japanese:
「そうだな。やっているのは、未来のための仲間作
　りだ」
lines.english: “That's right. What he's really doing is gathering allies for the future.”

lines.japanese:
「そして自分の考え方を、子供のうちに刷り込む。
　それが連中のやり方……古くから伝わる束ねの
　極意なんだ」
lines.english: “And planting his own ideas in them while they're still children. That's their method… the old secret of binding people together.”

lines.japanese: 「最上なりしは十年かけて作る友、ってな」
lines.english: “The best friend is one you spend ten years making, or so they say.”

lines.japanese: 「わかるけど……別に面白そうとは思わない」
lines.english: “I understand… but it doesn't sound like much fun.”

lines.japanese:
「そうか？　党に入るといろいろと守らないといけ
　ないことはできるが、イジメられなくなるぞ」
lines.english: “Maybe not. Join the Party and you get all kinds of rules to follow, but at least no one bullies you.”

lines.japanese:
「また同じ党で、下の人間を使うこともできる。
　手下みたいに」
lines.english: “And you get to order lower-ranking Party members around. Like underlings.”

lines.japanese: 「決まりに逆らえば、党の罰があるがな」
lines.english: “Break the rules and the Party punishes you, though.”

lines.japanese: 「……おやおや」
lines.english: “…Oh, my.”

lines.japanese:
「それは守ればいい。たいしたことじゃないさ。引
　き替えに安全を買える。出世すれば、いい目を見
　られる。誰だって入りたがる。そういうものだ」
lines.english: “Then obey them. It isn't hard. That buys you safety in return. Rise through the ranks and you're rewarded. Everyone wants in. That's how it works.”

lines.japanese: 「なるほどね」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「……少し、雰囲気が変わったか、おまえ？」
lines.english: “…Something about you changed just now, didn't it?”
“No—”

lines.japanese:
目頭を押さえる。
　表情から、浮かびかけていた険が消えた。
lines.english: He pressed his fingertips to the corners of his eyes. The hardness just beginning to show in his expression vanished.

lines.japanese: 「それで、他には？」
lines.english: “What else?”

lines.japanese:
「おまえには友達がいないようなので、話してる。
　知らないことで、怪我をすることもあるからな」
lines.english: “I'm telling you because you don't seem to have any friends. Not knowing this stuff can get you hurt.”

lines.japanese: 「党と関係ないヤツは狙われやすいんだ」
lines.english: “People with no connection to the Party make easy targets.”

lines.japanese: 「わかった。誰にも言うなってことだね」
lines.english: “I understand. You don't want me to tell anyone.”

lines.japanese: 「それがおまえのためだ」
lines.english: “It's for your own good.”

lines.japanese: 「了解。君から聞いたことは守秘する」
lines.english: “Understood. I will maintain confidentiality regarding anything you've told me.”

lines.japanese: 「しゅ、ひ？」
lines.english: “Confi… what?”

lines.japanese: 意味がわからないようだった。
lines.english: He seemed not to understand the word.

lines.japanese: 「……秘密にする」
lines.english: “…I'll keep it secret.”
“Oh…”

lines.japanese:
「どうやらおまえ、頭は悪くないらしいな。だった
　ら、そのうち声の一つもかかるかもな」
lines.english: “Looks like you’re not stupid. In that case, somebody might invite you sooner or later.”

lines.japanese: 「断ったらマズそうだね」
lines.english: “It sounds like saying no would be a bad idea.”

lines.japanese:
「そんなことはない。まあ……それから先、イジメ
　られても助けてはもらえないだろうけどな」
lines.english: “Not really. Although… if you get bullied afterward, no one's likely to help you.”

lines.japanese:
「そういうのを放っておくことで、党に入ることが
　良いことだって証明することになる」
lines.english: “By standing aside and letting that happen, the Party makes the case that you're better off joining.”

lines.japanese: 「怖くなったか？」
lines.english: “Scared now?”

lines.japanese:
「……かもね。
　今のところイジメられてはいないけど」
lines.english: “…Maybe. Nobody's bullying me yet, though.”

lines.japanese:
「でも、あまり楽しいチームだとは思わないよ、
　やっぱり」
lines.english: “But it still doesn't sound like a very fun group to me.”

lines.japanese:
「僕はこっちに越してきてから、ずっと一人のまま
　で、それは少し寂しい」
lines.english: “I've been alone ever since I moved here, and it does get a little lonely.”

lines.japanese:
「そんなのが続いたらやだなって思う。
　けど……党とかいうのに入るのは違うと思う」
lines.english: “I don't want things to stay that way. But… I don't think joining this Party is the answer.”
“……I see.”

lines.japanese: 斎から発せられていた疑惑が、少し薄まる。
lines.english: The suspicion in Itsuki's face softened a little.

lines.japanese:
「そういうこと、他の人間の前で言うな。誰が党員
　かわからないんだ」
lines.english: “Don't say that in front of anybody else. You never know who might be a Party member.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、気をつける」
lines.english: “All right. I'll be careful.”

lines.japanese:
斎は手にしたボールを葉子に放った。
　それは放物線を描いて、頭に当たった。
lines.english: Itsuki tossed the ball in his hand to Youko. It arced through the air and struck her on the head.
“Oh?”

lines.japanese:
転々と転がるボールをよたよたと追いかけていく。
　声が届かなくなるほど遠くまで。
lines.english: She wobbled after the ball as it bounced and rolled away— far enough that she could no longer hear them.

lines.japanese: 「……それとな」
lines.english: “…And one more thing.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「女を」
lines.english: “Girls…”

lines.japanese: 斎は言い淀んだ。
lines.english: Itsuki hesitated.

lines.japanese:
「いや、無理強いではないんだけどな……
　そのな、取り回してる」
lines.english: “No one forces them, exactly… but they get passed around.”

lines.japanese: 意識が揺れるほどの、衝撃だった。
lines.english: The shock sent Shinobu's mind reeling.

lines.japanese: 「集会と言われてな」
lines.english: “They call it a gathering.”

lines.japanese:
「参加できるのは、出世したヤツだけだ。年齢制限
　もあるぞ。俺たちと同学年まではアウトだ」
lines.english: “Only people who've moved up the ranks can go. There's an age limit too. Nobody our age or younger is allowed.”

lines.japanese: 「もちろん……できることが条件だしな」
lines.english: “And of course… they have to be able to do it.”

lines.japanese: 「意味、わかるか？」
lines.english: “Do you understand what I mean?”

lines.japanese: 「……ええと」
lines.english: “Um…”

lines.japanese: しばし考えて、
lines.english: Shinobu considered that for a moment.

lines.japanese: 「無理矢理ではないというのは？」
lines.english: “What do you mean, they aren't forced?”

lines.japanese:
「党員はもてるからな。その中でも、集会に出るこ
　とに抵抗のない女を選ぶ」
lines.english: “Party members are popular. They pick girls who don't mind going to the gatherings.”

lines.japanese: 「女の子が拒否したら？」
lines.english: “What if a girl refuses?”

lines.japanese:
「何もない。ただ出世はしにくくなる。逆に受け入
　れた女は、突然昇っていく。そういうのを見てる
　と、考えの変わる女もいるだろうな」
lines.english: “Nothing. It just gets harder for her to move up. A girl who agrees to it, on the other hand, can climb overnight. Watching that might change some girls’ minds.”

lines.japanese: 「この関係は兄弟っていう」
lines.english: “They call that kind of bond ‘brothers.’”

lines.japanese:
「兄弟っていうのは、この場合、姉・妹も含めるよ
　うなもので、男女は関係ない」
lines.english: “‘Brothers’ here includes older and younger sisters too. Being a boy or a girl has nothing to do with it.”

lines.japanese:
「つまり上の方の連中は、互いに兄弟関係にあるっ
　てことだ。互いに信頼してるし、仲間意識は強い」
lines.english: “In other words, the people near the top are all ‘brothers’ to one another. They trust each other, and their bond is strong.”

lines.japanese:
「仲間は絶対に見捨てないし、他の連中にやられた
　ら必ず報復する」
lines.english: “They never abandon their own. If someone from another group hurts one of them, they always retaliate.”

lines.japanese: 「そういうものだ」
lines.english: “That's how it works.”

lines.japanese: 「……なるほど」
lines.english: “…I see.”

lines.japanese: 「で、ここからが本題だけどな」
lines.english: “But here's the part that matters.”

lines.japanese:
「党の連中は、兄弟でなくとも互いにそれなりに強
　い結束があるんだ」
lines.english: “Even Party members who aren't brothers share a fairly strong bond.”

lines.japanese:
「入ったばかりのやつには、指導するために一個上
　の先輩がつくしな」
lines.english: “When someone first joins, a senior from the year above is assigned to show them the ropes.”

lines.japanese:
「他のクラス、他の学校のヤツらにも知り合いがで
　きる。どんどんと」
lines.english: “You get to know kids in other classes and other schools too. More and more of them.”

lines.japanese: 「……友達ってことだ」
lines.english: “…Friends, in other words.”

lines.japanese: ボールを手に、葉子が戻ってくる。
lines.english: Youko came back with the ball.

lines.japanese: 斎はボールを取り上げ、また遠くに投げた。
lines.english: Itsuki took it and threw it far away again.
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: またよたよたと走っていった。
lines.english: Again she tottered off after it.

lines.japanese: 「そういう友達の作り方も、ここにはあるんだ」
lines.english: “That's one way people make friends around here.”
“But…”

lines.japanese: 「俺は」
意図的に遮る口ぶりで、斎は言葉を続けた。
lines.english: Itsuki went on, deliberately cutting Shinobu off.

lines.japanese: 「党の一員だ」
lines.english: “I'm in the Party.”
“Huh…?”

lines.japanese:
「おまえを紹介してやることができる。といっても、
　俺も末端だから、同じく末端入党になるけどな」

lines.japanese: 最後の薬を飲んだ。
lines.english: He swallowed the last pill.

lines.japanese: 鎮痛剤はいつだって手放せない。
lines.english: He could never go without painkillers.

lines.japanese:
飲んだ直後だったせいで、効果があらわれてはい
なかったせいか、忍は奇妙な違和感を間近に見付けた。
lines.english: Perhaps because he had only just taken the pills and they had not yet begun to work, Shinobu noticed something subtly wrong nearby.

lines.japanese: 目を向ける。
lines.english: He looked.

lines.japanese: 集団である。
lines.english: A group.

lines.japanese:
一群となった若者の群れが、人の流れを切り分け
ている。
lines.english: A knot of young people, moving as one, cut across the flow of the crowd.

lines.japanese:
その連なる視線を、投じるように投げた先は……
貴宮忍個人であった。
lines.english: Every gaze in that group converged on… Shinobu Atemiya, and no one else.

lines.japanese:
腰が浮いた。
　顔を確認していく。
　全員、若いとはいっても忍より上の世代が多い。
lines.english: He rose from the barrier. He searched their faces. They were all young, but most were older than Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
年下はいないように見えた。
　知っている顔はない。……中央にいる一人をのぞ
いては。
lines.english: None appeared younger. Not one face was familiar… except the man at their center.

lines.japanese:
造作、というより雰囲気を記憶していた。
　かつて会ったときは、制服を身につけていた。
lines.english: Shinobu remembered the man's air more clearly than his features. When they had met before, the man had worn a school uniform.

lines.japanese:
そして滲み出る独特の念めいたもの……気配は、
まだこれほど“凶”に染まってはいなかった。
lines.english: And the peculiar will that seemed to seep from him—his presence— had not yet carried a ‘Sinister’ stain this deep.

lines.japanese:
その男―――すでに少年の域を脱している―――
が、歩み出る。
lines.english: The man—now well past boyhood— stepped forward.

lines.japanese:
統べる者。
　背後にいる連中をまとめあげているのが、その男
であることは間違いない。
lines.english: The one who ruled them. There could be no doubt that this was the man holding the people behind him together.

lines.japanese:
見ればわかる。
　周囲との格差がありすぎた。
lines.english: One look made that plain. The gulf between him and the others was too great.

lines.japanese: （この人の“密度”はなんだ？）
lines.english: (What is this man's ‘density’?)

lines.japanese: 忍は先ほど、心の強さについて思いを巡らせた。
lines.english: Only moments before, Shinobu had been thinking about strength of heart.

lines.japanese:
想像もつかない、怪物めいたものでしかない……
というのがひとまずの結論だ。
lines.english: His tentative conclusion had been that such strength was beyond imagining— something monstrous.

lines.japanese: だが眼前に立つ男は―――
lines.english: Yet the man standing before him—

lines.japanese: 「……貴宮忍か」
lines.english: “…Shinobu Atemiya.”

lines.japanese: 怪物が、声をかけてきた。
lines.english: The monster addressed him.

lines.japanese: 「僕の名前を……」
lines.english: “You know my name…”

lines.japanese: 「調べさせてもらった」
lines.english: “I had you investigated.”

lines.japanese:
門倉正道の凝らした双眼が、壁のように押しつけ
られた。
lines.english: Seidou Kadokura's unwavering gaze bore down on him like a wall.

lines.japanese: 「おまえのしたことも、把握している」
lines.english: “I also know what you did.”

lines.japanese:
「ずっと誉めてやりたかった。見事だったな。
　良くやったな」
lines.english: “I've been wanting to commend you for a long time. Magnificent. You did well.”

lines.japanese: 肩を叩き、愛おしげに揉む。
lines.english: He patted Shinobu’s shoulder, then squeezed it fondly.

lines.japanese:
「おまえのような人間を見いださねばならなかった
　のにな」
lines.english: “I should have found someone like you.”

lines.japanese:
対応を決めかねる。
　どういう態度で臨めば良いかもわからない。
　小市民の発想に、我ながら嫌になる。
lines.english: Shinobu could not decide how to answer. He did not even know how to conduct himself. His own petty-bourgeois thinking disgusted him.

lines.japanese: 「この位置まで戻るのに、ずいぶんと時間をかけた」
lines.english: “It took me a very long time to regain this position.”

lines.japanese: 「正直、最初の一年はおまえを憎んだよ」
lines.english: “To be honest, I hated you for the first year.”

lines.japanese:
「だが冷静になってみれば、単に俺が未熟であった
　だけのことだと、わかった」
lines.english: “But once I looked at it calmly, I realized I had simply been immature.”

lines.japanese: 「会ったら、一言誉めてやろうと思っていた」
lines.english: “I decided that if we ever met, I would offer you a word of praise.”

lines.japanese: 「たいしたやつだ。おめでとう、貴宮忍」
lines.english: “You're quite something. Congratulations, Shinobu Atemiya.”

lines.japanese: 「でな。一つ、聞きたい」
lines.english: “Now, there is one thing I want to ask.”

lines.japanese: 「……な、なんです？」
lines.english: “…W-what?”

lines.japanese: 「おまえはいったい何だ？」
lines.english: “What, exactly, are you?”

lines.japanese:
時間が止まる。
　ぬるりとうねる。
lines.english: Time stopped. Then it buckled in a slow, viscous wave.

lines.japanese: 「おまえの立場を調べた」
lines.english: “I investigated your circumstances.”

lines.japanese:
「おまえの病気について調べた。おまえの姉と呼ば
　れる人間について調べた。おまえの関わる組織に
　ついて調べた。その及ぶ力の度合いも調べた」
lines.english: “I investigated your illness. I investigated the person you call your sister. I investigated the organization you are involved with. I even investigated how far its power extends.”

lines.japanese:
「なるほど、確かにちょっとした権力の申し子のよ
　うなものだ。実態はしかし、可愛がられるモルモ
　ットといったところか」
lines.english: “Granted, you seem almost like a little prince of power. In reality, though, you're closer to a pampered guinea pig.”

lines.japanese:
「おまえ自身のものではない。アレは一世一代の
　我が儘を、通しただけのことだと知った」
lines.english: “That power isn’t yours. I learned that the whole affair was merely a once-in-a-lifetime whim forced through.”

lines.japanese: 「だが、それさえもごまかしだ」
lines.english: “But even that is misdirection.”

lines.japanese:
「核心を外している。そもそも、おまえが俺を射落
　とした理由からしてな」
lines.english: “That misses the heart of the matter. Starting with the very reason you shot me down.”

lines.japanese:
「斎に葉子は、我々にしてみれば多少なりとも意味
　のある駒だが、おまえにとって利となるものでも
　ないだろう」
lines.english: “Itsuki and Youko are pieces of some use to us, but I can hardly imagine they offered anything of value to you.”
“They were… my friends—”

lines.japanese: 「当時、おまえは斎と友人関係ではなかった」
lines.english: “At the time, you and Itsuki were not friends.”

lines.japanese: 刀で断つような物言いは、真実の重みをともなった。
lines.english: His words cut like a sword and carried the weight of truth.

lines.japanese: （情報が……正確だ）
lines.english: (His information… is accurate.)

lines.japanese:
舌を巻く。
　本当に調べ尽くしたようだ。
lines.english: Shinobu had to marvel. The man truly seemed to have investigated every last detail.

lines.japanese:
塀の中で調べたのだ。
　塀の外の駒を使ったのだ。
lines.english: He had conducted the investigation from inside the walls. He had used pieces on the outside.

lines.japanese: あの状況から―――
lines.english: From that position—

lines.japanese: 「驚いたか？　門倉はそれくらいの力はある」
lines.english: “Surprised? The Kadokuras command at least that much power.”

lines.japanese: 「草の根を洗うような真似だが、結果は出た」
lines.english: “It meant combing through every last blade of grass, but it produced results.”

lines.japanese:
手ずから育て、市井から人を取り上げるのだ。
　惰性であっても、それくらいは実現するのだろう。
lines.english: The family cultivated its own people, plucking them out of ordinary life. Even coasting on its own momentum, it could presumably manage that much.

lines.japanese: 「もう一度訊くが、おまえはなんだ？」
lines.english: “Let me ask you again. What are you?”

lines.japanese: 「何をもって、保護されている？」
lines.english: “What is it about you that earns their protection?”
“…A patient.”

lines.japanese: 「なるほど」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese:
予想していたと言わんばかりの態度に、忍は鼻白
んだ。
lines.english: Shinobu recoiled from Kadokura's air of having expected that answer all along.

lines.japanese: が、門倉は取り合うこともなく、背を向けた。
lines.english: Kadokura paid him no mind and turned his back.

lines.japanese: 「斎と葉子は、返してもらう」
lines.english: “I'm taking Itsuki and Youko back.”

lines.japanese:
「憤るか？　だがこれは元の鞘だ。おまえに飲まさ
　れた煮え湯の代価を求めたわけでもない、自然な
　結末だ」
lines.english: “Does that anger you? But all that's happening is that the sword is returning to its old scabbard. I'm not demanding payment for the way you burned me. It is the natural conclusion.”

lines.japanese: 「過去のことは、もはやどうでも良いことだからな」
lines.english: “What happened in the past no longer matters.”

lines.japanese: 「斎と葉子を、駒にするとあなたは言った」
lines.english: “You said you would turn Itsuki and Youko into your pieces.”

lines.japanese: 「なら……僕の行動も変わりませんよ」
lines.english: “Then… I won't be changing course either.”

lines.japanese:
再度の、政治的アプローチも辞さない。
　忍が言外に含ませた脅迫に門倉は、
lines.english: He was prepared to bring political pressure to bear again. Kadokura answered the threat implicit in Shinobu's words—

lines.japanese: 「それでいい。こちらが対処すれば済むことだ」
lines.english: “Good. Then we need only deal with it on our end.”

lines.japanese: 「同じ轍は踏まないつもりだが、踏んでも構わない」
lines.english: “I do not intend to repeat the same mistake. But if I do, so be it.”

lines.japanese:
「らしくあれと思うだけだ。
　らしく、最後までやるさ」
lines.english: “I only mean to remain true to myself. And true to myself, I'll see this through to the end.”

lines.japanese: 「…………そんなのは、駄目だ」
lines.english: “……That's no good.”

lines.japanese: 「駄目？」
lines.english: “No good?”

lines.japanese: 駆け引きも配慮もない言葉しかよこさなかった。
lines.english: Shinobu's reply held neither calculation nor tact.

lines.japanese: 「そんなことは通さない。斎も葉子も返さない」
lines.english: “I won't let you. I'm not giving Itsuki or Youko back.”

lines.japanese: 「“返さない”か」
lines.english: “You're ‘not giving them back,’ hm?”

lines.japanese: 首だけを巡らせた。
lines.english: He looked back over his shoulder.

lines.japanese:
「人の感触ばかりは会ってみなければわからないが、
　おまえは想像していたより、純然たるものではな
　いようだな」
lines.english: “You can never take the measure of a man without meeting him, but it seems you are less pure than I imagined.”

lines.japanese:
もはや敵意を隠すこともできない。
　鋭利さを増した双眸で、門倉を刺す。
lines.english: Shinobu could no longer conceal his hostility. His eyes, now sharper, stabbed at Kadokura.

lines.japanese:
が、厳のような背中は敵愾心を通すやわなもので
はなかったようだ。
lines.english: But Kadokura’s rocklike back seemed impervious to his hostility.

lines.japanese: 圧倒的な力の差。
lines.english: The overwhelming gulf in power.

lines.japanese: 「猟奇殺人については聞いているか？」
lines.english: “Have you heard about the bizarre murder case?”

lines.japanese: 唐突な話しぶり。忍は混乱する。
lines.english: The sudden change of subject confused Shinobu.

lines.japanese: 「手始めにその件を仕切る。斎を使う」
lines.english: “To begin with, I'll run that investigation. I'll use Itsuki.”

lines.japanese:
「止めたければやってみろ。ただし斎は説得には応
　じない。前回と同じルートでの圧力も無効とさせ
　ていただく。アドバイスを聞くか？」
lines.english: “Try to stop me if you can. But Itsuki will not be persuaded, and I will see to it that pressure through the same channels as last time has no effect. Would you care for some advice?”

lines.japanese: 「…………言いたいのなら」
lines.english: “…If you want to.”

lines.japanese: 「優位な自分の言葉に、酔いしれたいのなら」
lines.english: “If you want to get drunk on your own words now that you have the upper hand.”
“Heh…”

lines.japanese: 「おまえが、先に解決するんだな」
lines.english: “Then be the one to solve it first.”
“…What?”

lines.japanese:
「危険な仕事だ。斎は狂気と戦うのだからな。死ぬ
　かもしれないな」
lines.english: “It is dangerous work. Itsuki will be going up against madness. He may die.”

lines.japanese:
「だから、そうならぬよう、おまえが一足先に解決
　してみせればいい」
lines.english: “So if you want to keep that from happening, solve the case one step ahead of him.”

lines.japanese: 「それで斎は安全だ」
lines.english: “Then Itsuki will be safe.”

lines.japanese: 「……そんなのは……っ」
lines.english: “…But that's…!”

lines.japanese:
唇を噛む。
　おそらくは言うとおりなのだ。
　斎は説得には応じない。あのサムライは応じない。
lines.english: He bit his lip. Kadokura was probably right. Itsuki would not be persuaded. That samurai would not be persuaded.

lines.japanese:
圧力は効かない。もう効かない。警戒され対策さ
れた。
lines.english: Pressure would not work. Not anymore. They had seen it coming and taken precautions.

lines.japanese:
果てしなく積み上がっていく問題を、忍は絶望を
もって眺めるしかなかった。
lines.english: All Shinobu could do was look on in despair as problems piled up without end.

lines.japanese:
確かに……唯一の方策は、肩代わりしかないので
ある。
lines.english: It was true… The only course left was to shoulder the burden in Itsuki's place.

lines.japanese:
門倉正道は歩いていった。
　集団を率いて、流れに逆らい、去った。
lines.english: Seidou Kadokura walked away. At the head of the group, he vanished against the tide of the crowd.

lines.japanese:
力を吸われた者の様相で、忍は腰を車止めに落と
した。
lines.english: As if the strength had been sucked out of him, Shinobu sank back onto the traffic barrier.

lines.japanese:
額に触れる。
　べったりと、手が濡れた。
lines.english: He touched his forehead. His hand came away soaking wet.

lines.japanese:
胃が重い。
　ぐるぐるまわっている。
lines.english: His stomach felt heavy. It churned and spun.

lines.japanese: 「……忍さんじゃありませんか？」
lines.english: “…Shinobu, is that you?”
“Youko…”

lines.japanese: 思わず、彼女の手首を掴んだ。
lines.english: Before he knew it, he had seized her wrist.

lines.japanese: 「返さない」
lines.english: “I won't give you back.”

lines.japanese: 「はい？」
lines.english: “Pardon?”

lines.japanese: 「返したく、ない」
lines.english: “I don't… want to give you back.”

lines.japanese: 力をこめた。
lines.english: His grip tightened.

lines.japanese: この日、門倉正道は帰還を果たした―――
lines.english: That was the day Seidou Kadokura returned—

lines.japanese: 葉子とともに工場に来ると、斎がいた。
lines.english: When Shinobu arrived at the factory with Youko, Itsuki was there.
“Hey.”
“…” (raises hand)

lines.japanese: 「みんなはいないのか」
lines.english: “Is no one else here?”

lines.japanese: 「飲み物用意しますです」
lines.english: “I'll make us something to drink, I will.”

lines.japanese: 葉子が奥に消える。
lines.english: Youko disappeared into the back room.

lines.japanese: 「よろしく」
lines.english: “Thanks.”

lines.japanese:
鞄を放り投げ、椅子に座る。
　寡黙な斎と二人きりになるといよいよ会話は滞る。
lines.english: He tossed down his bag and took a seat. Alone with the taciturn Itsuki, conversation soon ground to a halt.

lines.japanese:
耳を澄ませば風鳴りの音が、鼓膜に掠れるほどに
意識できた。
lines.english: When he strained his ears, Shinobu could hear the wind just grazing his eardrums.

lines.japanese:
忍はこんな時間が嫌いではない。
　貴重な一瞬と、尊ぶべき記憶であった。
　が―――
lines.english: He did not mind times like these. Each was a precious instant, a memory to treasure. But—

lines.japanese:
「たまには静かなのもいいけど……
　今日は少し寂しいね」
lines.english: “A little quiet is nice now and then… but it feels lonely today.”

lines.japanese: 「……みんな、どうしてんのかな」
lines.english: “…I wonder what everyone's up to.”

lines.japanese: 「どうぞ」
lines.english: “Here you are.”

lines.japanese: お盆に乗せた三つのカップが、湯気を立てていた。
lines.english: Three cups stood steaming on her tray.

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう」
lines.english: “Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「昼間、誰か来てたみたいです」
lines.english: “It looks as though someone came by during the day.”

lines.japanese: 「本当？」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ。誰かお湯を沸かした形跡が」
lines.english: “Yes. Someone seems to have boiled water.”

lines.japanese: 「誰だろう？」
lines.english: “Who could it have been?”

lines.japanese: 「そこまでは……？」
lines.english: “That's all I can tell you…?”

lines.japanese:
「え？　日中に来ているとすれば章二しかいないっ
　て？　確かにそうだね……」
lines.english: “What? You think Shouji's the only one who'd come by during the day? You're right…”

lines.japanese: 目の端に、何かが止まった。
lines.english: Something caught his eye.
“…Huh?”

lines.japanese:
立ち上がり、それを手に取る。
　デパートの袋に入った、それは数枚の音楽ディス
クだった。
lines.english: He stood and picked it up. The department-store bag held several music CDs.

lines.japanese: 全てクラシックだ。
lines.english: All of them were classical.

lines.japanese: 「なんですか、それ？」
lines.english: “What is that?”

lines.japanese: 「章二に貸してたディスクだ」
lines.english: “They're CDs I lent Shouji.”

lines.japanese: メモが入ってる。
lines.english: There was a note inside.

lines.japanese: 『まあまあだった。こいつも聞いておけ』
lines.english: ‘Not bad. Listen to this one too.’

lines.japanese: 「あと、なんか貸してくれたみたい」
lines.english: “Looks like he lent me something of his, too.”

lines.japanese: 「音楽？」
lines.english: “Music?”

lines.japanese: 「そう」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「忍さんはイメージ通りですよね、クラシックとか」
lines.english: “Classical music and all that—you really are exactly as I pictured.”

lines.japanese: 「癒されるから」
lines.english: “It soothes me.”
“Soothing…”

lines.japanese: 瞳に妖しい光がともる。
lines.english: A dangerous gleam came into her eyes.

lines.japanese:
癒しといういかにもな単語が火をつけた。
　忍は無言で、そのまぶたをぐいぐい押した。
lines.english: That telltale little word, soothing, had struck a spark. Without a word, Shinobu pressed firmly on her eyelids.

lines.japanese: 「おうっ、おうっ」
lines.english: “Oof, oof.”

lines.japanese: スイッチが入る前に潰した形となった。
lines.english: He had crushed the impulse before her switch could flip.

lines.japanese: 「章二も聞くんだよね、これがまた」
lines.english: “The funny thing is, Shouji listens to this stuff too.”

lines.japanese: 平然と元の流れに。
lines.english: And just like that, he returned to the subject.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと腹だたしいですよね」
lines.english: “That is a little irritating.”

lines.japanese: 「そうかな。意外と合ってるようにも思うけど」
lines.english: “Is it? I think it suits him surprisingly well.”

lines.japanese: 「聞いてみますか？」
lines.english: “Shall we listen?”

lines.japanese: 「だね」
lines.english: “Let's.”

lines.japanese:
新しく借りたディスクを、プレイヤーにセットし
ようとする。
lines.english: He went to put the newly borrowed CD into the player.

lines.japanese: 「では」
lines.english: “Here goes.”

lines.japanese: ところが、電源が入らない。
lines.english: But the player would not turn on.

lines.japanese: 「あ、電池切れてるんでした、それ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. The batteries are dead.”

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: 「買ってくれば良かったな」
lines.english: “I should've picked some up.”

lines.japanese: 「……行ってきましょうか？」
lines.english: “…Shall I go and buy some?”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ。そんなことしないで」
lines.english: “No. You don't need to do that.”

lines.japanese: 斎が立ち上がる。
lines.english: Itsuki stood.

lines.japanese:
「え？　斎が行くって？
　いいって、そんなの。またのときで」
lines.english: “What? You'll go, Itsuki? No, really. We can listen some other time.”

lines.japanese:
「いいからいいから。妹の淹れてくれたコーヒーを

「珍しいですね。
